I’m an AI engineer and I’m right now building ChatMakr, an AI-powered platform that creates multi-agent chatbots in seconds. I also built Rune Score, a sports analytics chatbot, and it cost me $0.

From the outside, it looks like a simple chatbot. Under the hood, it’s a distributed system that has to handle the freshness of sports data, user rephrasing, extraction failures, LLM call costs, streaming, memory, fallbacks and security. Here’s the stack I actually used to build it layer by layer, what I did with each tool and what’s free about it.

Before writing a line of code, a chatbot needs a face. I used Figma to generate the chatbot’s logo straight from a text prompt describing the style and mood I wanted, then iterated on it a few times inside Figma itself rather than handing it to a designer. Figma’s own free blueprint covers individual use with unlimited file storage.

According to recent reports, the whole project lives in a GitHub repository, private while the chatbot was still rough, and it’s the same repo both Claude and Codex connect to. GitHub’s free blueprint gives unlimited private repositories with a limited feature set and 2,000 minutes a month of Actions included on GitHub Free for standard runners on private repos, enough to run tests and basic automation without hitting a wall. Standard runners on public repositories stay free no matter how much you use them.

Claude Code did the actual building, the chatbot’s backend and the AI agents running inside it. I kept it connected directly to the GitHub repository and never let it touch the main branch directly: every task ran on its own branch, and nothing merged until I’d reviewed the diff myself and approved the pull request. The genuine free route in is a Guest Pass: if someone you know already pays for Claude Max, they can send you one, and it unlocks a full week of free Pro-level access.

According to recent reports, I gave Codex a different job, connected to the same repository but never writing production code itself. It reviewed what Claude had actually shipped, acting as an independent judge on pull requests, and I also used it to draft the next development prompt I’d hand back to Claude, effectively having one model proposal the work and another execute it. Codex has a genuine free plan at $0 a month. Free accounts run on GPT-5.6 Terra, OpenAI’s cost-efficient model for that tier. The free plan is capped at a usage limit rather than a time limit, which is exactly the size of job a reviewer role needs.

According to recent reports, I bought the chatbot’s domain name through Cloudflare, where registration is usually cheap since Cloudflare sells at cost with no markup, and kept the DNS in the same place rather than splitting it across providers. From there I used Cloudflare’s free security layer to protect the domain, including rate limiting rules to stop any single source from hammering the chatbot’s endpoints. Cloudflare’s WAF documentation covers exactly this kind of rule, and the core protections, DNS, DDoS protection, and basic security features, are included on the free plan.

I used Railway for both the backend and the frontend, with a separate test environment so I could ship changes quickly without risking the live version. Upcoming accounts get a one-time free credit grant before any card is required, and unlike some free hosts, Railway doesn’t put your service to sleep by default the way its own documentation describes for its optional Serverless feature, so there’s no cold start tax on the free tier unless you turn that behavior on yourself.

It has been revealed that conversations, users and application data all sit in Neon, a serverless Postgres database that scales down to zero and stops costing anything the moment nobody’s using it. The free tier includes enough storage and monthly compute hours for a real early product, with no credit card required to start.

According to recent reports, once the chatbot’s AI agents were actually running, I needed to see what they were doing under the hood: which prompts fired, where they failed, and what they cost. Langfuse traces all of that, and its free Hobby proposal includes a healthy monthly allowance of tracing events, enough to debug and monitor a real chatbot without paying anything.

According to recent reports, I wired Exa and Firecrawl directly into the AI agents responsible for research inside the chatbot’s runtime, so the chatbot itself can decide when it needs to look something up. Exa handles the search, finding relevant pages for a given question, and its free tier hands newly introduced accounts starting credit plus a recurring monthly allowance with no payment method required. It also ships a playground where you can test a search query directly in the browser before wiring it into your agent. Firecrawl handles what comes next, turning a page Exa found into clean text the agent can actually read, and its own free blueprint includes a monthly credit allowance with no card needed either.

Before committing to a specific model for the chatbot’s agents, I used NVIDIA’s API Catalog to try several without paying per token. NVIDIA gives any developer free credits to test a wide range of hosted models through its own endpoints, which made it easy to compare options before locking in whichever one actually powers the chatbot in production.

Sources indicate that the chatbot talks back, not just types, so I used Azure AI Speech for text to speech, letting the chatbot switch between a female or male neural voice depending on the setup. The free tier includes a real monthly allowance of neural voice characters at no cost, enough for genuine daily conversations before you’d ever see a bill.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Silicon Motion is showing off its PCIe 6.0 SSD controller for data center applications for the first time at the SC26 conference in Chicago.
  • Sources indicate that silicon Motion introduced its high-end MonTitan SM8466 enterprise SSD controller designed for next-generation data center and hyperscale storage applications at FMS 2025.
  • Recent findings suggest that to improve performance and reduce latency, Silicon Motion has developed its Separate Command Architecture (SCA), which separates command and address transmission paths within the NAND interface to improve parallelism and increase effective throughput.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silicon Motion is showing off its PCIe 6.0 SSD controller for data center applications for the first time at the SC26 conference in Chicago. The final iteration of Silicon Motion's SM8466 controller was taped out recently, and drives based on the chip are due in late 2027 or early 2028. However, the latest controller also has a secret weapon designed to ensure consistent performance of SSDs under concurrent workloads that may set it apart from competitors.

Sources indicate that silicon Motion introduced its high-end MonTitan SM8466 enterprise SSD controller designed for next-generation data center and hyperscale storage applications at FMS 2025. The controller features a PCIe 6.x x4 host interface and 16 NAND channels to enable sequential transfer speeds of up to 28 GB/s, random performance of up to 7 million 4K IOPS, and capacities of up to 512 TB and beyond as newer 3D NAND devices emerge. Just like other high-end data center-grade SSD controllers released in recent years, the SM8466 complies with NVMe 2.0 and OCP NVMe 2.5 SSD specifications.

Recent findings suggest that to improve performance and reduce latency, Silicon Motion has developed its Separate Command Architecture (SCA), which separates command and address transmission paths within the NAND interface to improve parallelism and increase effective throughput. Additionally, the controller supports Silicon Motion's 2nd Generation PerformaShape technology, which enables programmable performance limits and predictable quality of service (QoS) across concurrent workloads, which is arguably its most key differentiator against rivals who rely on different methods of guaranteeing performance.

According to recent reports, in addition to its performance chops, the MonTitan SM8466 incorporates advanced error correction, virtualization, data protection, and security features. The controller's error correction engine supports low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with 4KiB codewords and Silicon Motion's 16KiB Collaborative Codeword (CoCo) technology to improve data integrity and reliability with advanced NAND flash memory. The controller also supports Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV), MPF virtualization, SMART diagnostics, and comprehensive data protection mechanisms. Security capabilities include Secure Boot, AES-256 encryption, TCG Opal compatibility, and firmware attestation. Together, these features make the SM8466 suitable for high-capacity data center drives that are expected to deliver high performance, predictable latency, and reliable operation under demanding data center workloads.

Industry observers note that silicon Motion's 2nd Generation PerformaShape technology builds upon the original PerformaShape architecture introduced with the firm's PCIe 5.0-based MonTitan SM8366 enterprise SSD controller several years ago. The 1st Generation implementation uses dedicated hardware accelerators and two-stage leaky-bucket regulators to control read and write performance in terms of IOPS and throughput, both for individual workloads and for the SSD as a whole. This approach enables data center operators to prevent one workload from monopolizing SSD resources at the expense of others.

PerformaShape 2 retains these capabilities but doubles the number of supported quality-of-service (QoS) sets from 256 to 512 and introduces more sophisticated performance controls to accommodate a larger number of concurrent workloads with different requirements. One of the key additions to PerformaShape 2 is Multi-Dimensional Shaping, which enables the controller to coordinate performance limits across multiple I/O characteristics rather than enforce each limit independently. This gives data center operators greater flexibility when allocating SSD resources among applications with different performance requirements.

Another key enhancement of PerformaShape 2 is support for NVMe TP4176, a proposed extension to the NVMe specification that aims to standardize performance management and QoS controls. Whereas the original PerformaShape relies on Silicon Motion's vendor-specific NVMe commands and a dedicated host driver, TP4176 could eventually enable compatible host software to configure performance policies through a standardized mechanism. The technology is particularly relevant for cloud environments where SSDs serve numerous virtual machines, containers, and applications whose storage requirements can change considerably over time, according to the company.

According to recent reports, anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them?
  • Recent findings suggest that the technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results.
  • Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising newly introduced method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.

Recent findings suggest that the technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.

A Upcoming Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy.

It has been revealed that the breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.

Industry observers note that quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can rapidly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.

In a recent development, but quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," states Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties.".

Rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the fresh approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify key interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.

"From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy.".

Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator.

It has been revealed that to evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.

Industry observers note that after this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, showed that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.

This represents an key step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.

Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems.

The next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.

"This is particularly important because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important.".

The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.

Looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.

It has been revealed that "After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," states Peter Zoller.

It has been revealed that this shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how quickly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.

The findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, NASA debuted a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration.

Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical technology.

NASA’s Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge is offering $500,000, split between two winning U.S. companies, to accelerate the maturation of mid-power systems that could be foundational to supporting future NASA and commercial missions. Interested parties can learn more at an AMPERE Virtual Industry Day hosted by NASA on Thursday, Nov. 19.

Industry observers note that “This challenge approach seeks to remove key barriers and facilitate commercialization by providing access to NASA subject matter expertise, state-of-the-art technologies, and world-class facilities at no cost to challenge winners,” noted Dr. Jason Frieman, AMPERE project co-owner at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland. “We hope participants will see this as an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities to NASA and other government and commercial stakeholders.”.

The competition is the first of NASA’s Tech Maturation Prize series, which seeks to accelerate development of breakthrough technologies in support of NASA missions while strengthening the U.S. space economy.

Recent findings suggest that the competition includes three phases. In Phase 1, each participating team will submit a concept design, manufacturing blueprint, and cost and performance projections. NASA may select two winners to advance to Phase 2, where teams will develop prototypes and collaborate with NASA personnel. Through no-cost licensing, these teams can gain early access to NASA-developed Hall effect thruster technologies that use krypton as a propellant. In Phase 3, prototypes will be tested at NASA Glenn at no cost to the participating teams.

In total, two winning teams may be selected to receive up to $250,000 each.

According to recent reports, the AMPERE Challenge is open for registration until Jan. 27, 2027, at 5 p.m. EST. The challenge supports the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket project, managed by NASA Glenn and NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The project is funded by the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. Yet2 administers the challenge through a contract with the NASA Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation within the Research and Technology Mission Directorate.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby.

Recent findings suggest that saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length.

Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

Industry observers note that the moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior.

Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant, along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025.

Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan, Dione, Tethys, Rhea and Iapetus.

#138. Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1268 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function.
  • The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time.
  • The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.

The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.

These questions are especially crucial because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.

More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills.

One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.

Industry observers note that cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn fresh things, and solve problems. These abilities play an key role in school performance and everyday decision-making.

It has been revealed that the findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.

"The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.

"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.

Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently.

The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.

Among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.

Working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing new information.

In a recent development, light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.

According to recent reports, the differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.

Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity.

The study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.

Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.

One possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.

This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.

"Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.

Recent findings suggest that "However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is key to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing.".

What the Eight-Year Study Revealed.

The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.

It has been revealed that the current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.

According to recent reports, researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.

To evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.

In a recent development, importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the results offer an crucial perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.

The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.

Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.

The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.

Sources indicate that pakistan's telecommunications authority, the PTA, has confirmed that internet connectivity complications affecting the country's residents are related to the failure of an international submarine cable. SEA-ME-WE 5 is located almost seven miles off the coast of Pakistan, near the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, and connects the region with European networks via the Middle East. The TWA says that the outage may have caused intermittent connectivity issues and a decline in service quality, with Transworld Associates (TWA) working to identify the cause of the issue. No timeframe has been provided for when a fix will be available yet, but for now, internet traffic has been rerouted to minimize the impact of the outage.

According to recent reports, the outage comes weeks after the Islamic Republic of Iran described several undersea fiber cables that run through the Strait of Hormuz as "legitimate upcoming targets" in the ongoing tensions in the area. February's start of military action by the United States, Israel, and others has made the Strait of Hormuz a household name in recent months. General Hossein Mohebbi, a spokesman for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, pointed out that as many as seven "large cables pass beneath the Strait of Hormuz, and all internet and commercial data pass through them," going on to say they are "legitimate" targets for the group.

One of the international submarine cable systems, the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5), have reported a fault at about 11 KM from Pakistan shore which may cause some internet users to experience intermittent connectivity concerns and a decline in service quality. Transworld Associates (TWA) is coordinating with the SMW5 Consortium to identify the root cause of the fault and determine the Estimated Time for Restoration (ETTR). In the meantime, internet traffic is being rerouted through alternative international links to minimise the impact and ensure service continuity to the greatest extent possible. #SMW5 #SubmarineCableFault #InternetDisruption #InternetUpdate #PakistanInternet #ConnectivityUpdate #InternetServices #DigitalPakistan #PTA #TransworldAssociates #TelecomUpdate #NetworkRestoration #StayConnected #InternetConnectivityNovember 18, 2026.

Sources indicate that notably, the SEA-ME-WE 5 cable does run through the Strait of Hormuz, although it should be stressed that there is at the moment no indication that this outage was caused by any act of sabotage. However, that is no doubt something that the TWA investigation will seek to confirm before it can apply whatever fix is necessary to fully restore services for those in the region.

Undersea cables are vital for maintaining connectivity between nations and continents, and Iran isn't the only one to have taken note. A Russian ship was chased from British waters by a Royal Navy attack helicopter earlier this year after it was found less than a mile from five undersea cables. The ship was in the area for 14 hours, and the cables it was near happened to connect the UK with Spain, Portugal, Canada, and the United States.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that holidays are often a fun break during a busy year – a long weekend here and there is an event many of us can get behind. However, when a short holiday break turns into a full holiday season, we know that this is a different “ball game”.

Everyone has stress about something – some people love the holidays, and some people are holiday-avoidant… and some live in the middle. What specific stressors or challenges you experience might not bother your sibling, your spouse or your coworker. We want to be aware of and have a clear understanding of what holidays mean to you as a person.

It has been revealed that the first step is to acknowledge what your feelings and emotions are – you may enjoy seeing the neighborhood holiday lights but not want to decorate yourself (totally okay!!), you may love shopping for the perfect gift for everyone on your list, you may avoid all of the activities — everyone one of these is an okay choice… you can be yourself always in all ways. Give yourself that permission. As you prepare, keep a list or a calendar of events – expected/obligated, okay to go or not go,.

It has been revealed that combine this with your standard calendar and make a schedule. If you want, add to the list what your part is (bring a dish, gift, coordinate a visit, etc.). Having the majority of activities written down will help you not overbook, help you proposal ahead, make it easier to say no, spend within your budget. Before you commit to something, say “I have to check my calendar first…. I will get back to you”.

Prepare your budget – We often budget for gifts but forget that we will be buying more groceries for those special meals and favorite dishes…. We also need to budget for travel, having guests in your home, clothing, even allow for a higher electric bill. Write it down – keep receipts – let your immediate family know that this is what we have to spend, then track it as you go.

Sources indicate that now that you have a current calendar and a working budget, set realistic expectations for your holiday experience. We know that not everything is optional and traditions will continue but none of it has to be perfect…minor stress and family friction can be normal.

It has been revealed that when telling someone no, use “I” statements and stick to the single concern at hand. In addition to your list/calendar, remember to prioritize time for yourself. Keep your regular sleep schedule as much as possible, eat well (if you have a heavy meal one day, lighten up the next), schedule time to get fresh air and a quick break. ALWAYS focus on what matters. Focus on meaningful connections rather than activities that cause you anxiety.

If you feel emotional, take a few moments alone and identify the feeling, honor yourself for being able to face it and breathe through it (avoid pushing it down). Remember how many times you have gotten through a “pressure moment” and give yourself credit. Call a trusted friend or your therapist if you feel overwhelmed for longer than a day….and, please call 988 if you feel overwhelmed to an extreme. 988 is always available and waiting to help.

Look for the glimmers – find a happy moment (no matter how brief), find the memories that make you smile. Thinking of something joyful changes your emotional state… train yourself to do this any time you need a lift. Ultimately, we want to move away from focusing on the future (It causes anxiety) or overthinking about the past (it causes depression) ….and find yourself in the here and now where you have power to manage things happening around you. Your power is with you in the present. (Eckert Tolle book – The Power of Now).

The holiday season lasts for weeks – gift yourself with.

In a recent development, person sitting on sofa next to a holiday tree. With the extra pressure of the holiday season, our feelings can often be stronger than other times during the year…. if you start having feelings: Anxious – take deep breaths, focus ONLY on the present – your surroundings, what you see, count objects, put ice on the inside of your wrists (this works really well!) Angry – walk away for a moment, take a break, give yourself as long as you need to regulate these feelings, know that whoever gets angry first loses…be the winner in the moment. Helpless, hopeless, trapped (discouraged) – remember that you have a voice, it is sometimes difficult to use it in family situations, but you can talk to yourself. Remember how strong you are, how many accomplishments you have completed…. reframe the situation so you recall all of your wonderful qualities. Overwhelmed – Check your list/holiday calendar again…what can you change or take off the list. What can you postpone for 24-48 hours? What can you give someone else to do? What can you order from the store rather than do the cooking or shopping yourself? Find a quick solution for one or two things (at least) and take some pressure off. Grief – acknowledge how you feel, we do not have to be cheerful just because it is a holiday. Say no to any event or activity that feels too “heavy” and give yourself permission to leave if it becomes too much. Find a way to keep their memory with you – carry a favorite picture or memento. Find a grief support group. Basically, we want to notice the small things and find gratitude in what we have. Our outward situation does not define us. If you find that holiday time is difficult or stressful, always give yourself permission to contact your EAP services for assistance and support.

#133. The Inventory Accuracy Problem Smart Fulfillment Centers Still Need To Solve

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1025 w)

The Inventory Accuracy Problem Smart Fulfillment Centers Still Need To Solve

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amruth Puppala | Senior Engineering Manager | Walmart.
  • In a recent development, ​Walk into a modern fulfillment center, and you will see how much warehouse operations have changed.
  • Yet, even with these advances, a familiar problem remains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amruth Puppala | Senior Engineering Manager | Walmart.

In a recent development, ​Walk into a modern fulfillment center, and you will see how much warehouse operations have changed. Robots move products, software coordinates thousands of orders and inventory systems track merchandise across receiving, storage and shipping.

Yet, even with these advances, a familiar problem remains.

It has been revealed that A system demonstrates that an item is available, but when someone goes to pick it, the product is not there. The inventory record may be correct on paper, but the physical reality is different. What seems like a minor discrepancy can quickly turn into additional searches, picking delays, order reallocation or missed shipping commitments.

In a recent development, this raises an key question. Instead of simply knowing how much inventory we have, shouldn’t we also know how reliable that information is?

Fulfillment centers and distribution centers handle enormous volumes of inventory movements every day. Products are received, stored, replenished, picked and shipped, often through a combination of manual processes and automated equipment.

Even with well-designed systems, discrepancies can occur.

A pallet may be placed in the wrong location. A receiving transaction might be completed before the merchandise is physically verified. Damaged inventory may not be removed from available stock immediately. Sometimes, a picking exception is recorded without the underlying inventory issue being resolved.

Warehouses already have processes to investigate these situations. Cycle counting, reconciliation and exception management are essential parts of daily operations.

However, many discrepancies are discovered only after they begin affecting order fulfillment.

By that point, the operations team is responding to a problem rather than preventing it.

One idea worth exploring is assigning a confidence score to inventory records based on the operational evidence supporting them.

Consider two storage locations, each showing 100 units available. The first location was recently verified, and its last several picking transactions were completed successfully. The second location has experienced repeated picking failures, unexplained quantity adjustments and an unresolved exception.

Both locations show the same available quantity, but they clearly do not carry the same level of operational confidence.

Today, many inventory decisions focus primarily on quantity, location and availability. Adding a confidence score could give warehouse systems another useful signal when making those decisions.

The score would not represent a latest inventory balance. It would indicate how much confidence the system has in the existing record.

This could help teams identify which locations need verification and which inventory discrepancies are most likely to affect upcoming orders.

Recent advances in AI create an opportunity to evaluate these signals continuously rather than relying entirely on scheduled checks.

A system could monitor receiving transactions, inventory movements, picking results and adjustment history to identify patterns that deserve attention.

For example, repeated picking failures at the same location might suggest a discrepancy. An unusual sequence of inventory adjustments could indicate a process matter. A location that has not been physically verified for an extended period could warrant additional scrutiny, particularly if the inventory is needed for upcoming shipments.

Rather than treating each event independently, the system could examine the broader history and determine whether further verification is justified.

Newer AI models can also help interpret exception notes and other information that traditional rule-based systems may struggle to analyze consistently. Where cameras or robotic sensors are available, their observations could provide additional supporting evidence.

The key point is that AI should help identify where to investigate, not make inventory adjustments without verification.

Cycle counting is one area where this approach could have immediate practical value.

Most distribution centers already use scheduled counting programs, often based on inventory value, product movement or operational requirements. Those methods are useful and should continue.

However, a fixed schedule does not always account for problems developing during the day.

Industry observers note that imagine a location that reports 100 units in stock. Several picking attempts fail within a short period, but the inventory quantity remains unchanged. Instead of waiting for the next scheduled count, the system could recommend that the location be checked sooner. The priority could increase if those units are needed for orders approaching their shipping cutoff.

Recent findings suggest that this would allow inventory teams to focus attention where a potential discrepancy is most likely to cause operational disruption. It could also help avoid unnecessary checks in locations where recent transactions consistently support the recorded inventory.

Sources indicate that I would not recommend introducing another large platform to solve this problem. Most warehouses already generate much of the information needed. The opportunity is to make better use of it.

A practical starting point would be to combine inventory movement history, picking exceptions, recent count results and upcoming order demand.

Sources indicate that simple rules could first identify obvious discrepancies. Machine learning could then help recognize less predictable patterns, while newer language models could assist with interpreting operational notes and explaining why a location has been flagged.

The warehouse management system would remain responsible for inventory records and transactions. Any quantity correction would continue through established verification and approval processes.

For an initial rollout, I would focus on a limited number of high-volume locations and measure whether the approach reduces repeated picking failures, shortens discrepancy resolution time and improves verification productivity.

Accuracy matters, but so does the amount of additional work introduced. If the system generates too many unnecessary checks, it has not solved the underlying problem.

Fulfillment technology has made progress in improving speed, automation and visibility. But visibility alone does not guarantee accuracy.

A warehouse can have a view of its recorded inventory and still make the wrong fulfillment decision when those records do not match physical conditions.

The next opportunity is to make inventory reliability a continuous part of warehouse operations, rather than something evaluated through periodic reconciliation.

Sources indicate that the goal is not to eliminate inventory discrepancies. That would be unrealistic in a continuously operating facility. The goal is to recognize problems earlier, direct people to locations and prevent disruptions before they affect customer orders.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The holiday shopping season is in full swing — and it started early this year.
  • Latest data from specialized point-of-sale software organization Quilt Software, which serves more than 20,000 independent retailers, from jewelers and pet stores to liquor stores and grocers, revealed a 7.6% same-store sales growth spike in October year over year.
  • That’s in stark contrast to the Q1 through Q3 2.7% to 3.2% bump, which might largely be attributed to inflation, Quilt Software co-founder and CEO Andrew Stern tells Entrepreneur.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The holiday shopping season is in full swing — and it started early this year.

Latest data from specialized point-of-sale software organization Quilt Software, which serves more than 20,000 independent retailers, from jewelers and pet stores to liquor stores and grocers, revealed a 7.6% same-store sales growth spike in October year over year.

That’s in stark contrast to the Q1 through Q3 2.7% to 3.2% bump, which might largely be attributed to inflation, Quilt Software co-founder and CEO Andrew Stern tells Entrepreneur.

According to recent reports, what’s more, customers aren’t just getting a head start; they’re also making more frequent shopping trips. Year-over-year transactions per store grew 6% in Q3 and 7.9% in October, per Quilt’s data.

This year, Small Business Saturday, which saw an estimated $18 billion in spending at independent retailers in 2025, falls on November 28, just 27 days before Christmas.

With customers opting for earlier and more frequent purchasing, independent retailers that want to make the most of the limited window need to stay on top of which items are selling in real time to remain ahead of trends and maintain inventory, Stern notes.

The CEO also cautions independent shops against attempting to compete with significant-box retailers like Amazon or Walmart on price or convenience, calling it a “race to the bottom.”.

Instead, Stern suggests a two-pronged approach for independent retailers: Lean into what makes them special, and use AI in a way that works for them (it won’t look like it does for mega-retailers).

“ For our small independent merchants, they opened their store for a reason,” Stern indicates. “They thought they were bringing something really unique that no one else had. So lean into that, because you’re probably right.”.

One in five holiday shoppers strategy to purchase gifts and other holiday items at small or local businesses this year, according to the National Retail Federation’s (NRF) October Holiday Consumer survey.

Shoppers planning to buy from small businesses cited reasons including supporting the community (71%), seeking unique gifts and décor (56%), championing artists through handmade purchases (37%) and finding high-quality products (33%), per the report.

It’s clear that holiday shoppers want what independent retailers have to offer — but it’s crucial that those stores put themselves on people’s radar.

Recent findings suggest that “ Make sure that [customers] can see you, that you’re visible when people do their Google searches, or increasingly their ChatGPT searches,” Stern states. “Make sure that you come up because they want to find you.”.

It has been revealed that nowadays, independent retailers must have an answer engine optimization (AEO) strategy to stay relevant and show up in search results. Earlier this month, Entrepreneur spoke with Courtney Sandora, founder of digital marketing agency Go Social, to learn more about how brands can compete in the AEO landscape.

Sandora notes that customers use LLM-powered search engines to ask specific questions, so savvy businesses should hone in on the queries they can reliably and successfully own, “seeding” stories and copy that bolster their authority.

“That storytelling extends across everything from PR to creators, even how you appear on a retailer website,” Sandora says. “Typically, on retailer websites, there’s a short description. Is the message you want to tell in that retailer website description? Consistency matters.”.

It’s critical that small businesses use rapidly advancing AI technologies to their advantage.

However, that won’t look exactly like it does for major retailers, which might harness AI to manage six-month supply chains or optimize warehouse logistics, Stern says.

Instead, independent retailers should focus on taking small steps with significant impact, like using agentic solutions to outsource specific tasks they might not have time to execute to their fullest potential.

In a recent development, for example, the right AI tool can give shop owners the marketing support they’ve never had, unfolding in the background as they help customers at the counter. Quilt offers its retailers an AI marketing assistant that can create campaigns for customers with their own inventory.

It has been revealed that “ This generative AI is able to create copy that’s in their voice,” Stern claims, “that’s tailored to different cohorts of customers and can say, ‘Hey, come in, I think we have some products that you might be interested in. Here they are.’”.

Quilt also offers an AI assistant that can help small retailers navigate unwieldy piles of inventory.

It has been revealed that stern points to thrift stores, which tend to rely on volunteer staff to sift through large amounts of donations promptly, as an example. Shops can snap a picture of a leather couch and receive a price estimate immediately.

Industry observers note that the AI tool can also help them identify rare and valuable items that might otherwise go unnoticed. “ We’ve had some crazy cases like, ‘Oh, that looks like a Tiffany lamp. Look at the bottom of it and see if there’s a signature that claims Tiffany. If so, do not charge $5 for that lamp,’” Stern says.

The NRF expects retail sales in November and December to grow 4.2% over 2025, for a total spending surpassing $1 trillion. That’s a massive opportunity for independent retailers that opt out of competition with big-box retailers and leverage the data to win their share.

Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5. Why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere said Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all. "The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere said. No such arrangement is in place for PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox. Ampere mentioned there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5.

Why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere stated Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all.

Beyond this, Ampere said there could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6 streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger position to serve a large influx of users streaming a brand-latest game like GTA 6 compared to Sony.".

"The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere stated. "While PS5 users can generally stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience.".

Beyond all this, Ampere highlighted how PS5 customers ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580) over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more key to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere stated.

Industry observers note that xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere remarked the total cost to play on Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6, a controller, and a screen.

Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be 0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming, assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game.

This rate leaves little margin for Xbox, Ampere stated, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in accounts that is never used.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23.

Recent findings suggest that filled with approximately 11,000 pounds of cargo, the Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL spacecraft, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The mission is known as NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25.

Sources indicate that after arriving at the International Space Station, NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, who are living and working aboard the space station, will use the Canadarm2 robotic arm to capture the Cygnus XL on Tuesday, Dec. 1. Ground controllers then will install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading.

Industry observers note that NASA’s live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:.

Highlights of space station research and technology demonstrations being delivered aboard this Cygnus XL spacecraft include experiments to improve drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis, predict cancer spread, and advance treatments for muscle loss, as well as improve radiation sensing and advance food production for future long-duration missions.

The spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the orbiting laboratory until May 2027, then depart with several thousand pounds of disposal items and other unneeded cargo, burning up harmlessly during re-entry.

Recent findings suggest that northrop Grumman named the spacecraft the S.S. James “Jim” A. Lovell in honor of the former NASA astronaut. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon.

12 p.m.: Prelaunch teleconference will stream on NASA’s YouTube channel with the following participants:.

To participate in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom for call details by 11 a.m., Nov. 23, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. The agency’s media credentialing policy is available online.

Additional prelaunch updates will be available on NASA’s space station blog.

10:25 a.m.: Launch coverage begins.

1:10 a.m.: Arrival coverage begins.

Sources indicate that launch day coverage of the mission will be available on the NASA website. Coverage will include live streaming and blog updates beginning no earlier than 10 a.m. on Nov. 29, as the countdown milestones occur. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, said on Thursday that yields of chips made using the organization's latest 18A (1.8nm-class) fabrication process have achieved 70%, which is more or less in line with what one would expect from an all-new manufacturing technology at this stage of its ramp. In addition, Intel and Microsoft have signed an agreement under which Microsoft will secure Intel Xeon supply capacity for years to come and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for in-house silicon.

"When I took over [as CEO in March, 2025], 18A yield was horrible; now we are at 70%," Lip-Bu Tan said at the TomorrowX conference (via @firesidealpha).

Lip-Bu Tan did not specify whether he meant functional yield, parametric yield, or percentage of sellable silicon. However, it is reasonable to expect a CEO of a semiconductor company to talk about functional die yield, the percentage of dies that pass basic electrical and functional testing.

Industry observers note that intel began volume production of compute tiles of its Core Ultra 300-series CPUs codenamed Panther Lake using 18A in the second half of 2025, so a 70% functional yield seems decent at this stage of the product ramp, though for Intel's economics a lot depends on parametric yield and how many advanced SKUs of Core Ultra 300-series 'Panther Lake' processors Intel can supply to customers at a premium. The same applies to Intel's Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest processors with up to 288 cores that are in high-volume production now and which use 18A-based compute chiplets along with Foveros Direct 3D stacking.

In addition to announcing an important 18A milestone, Intel also signed a long-term agreement with Microsoft, under which the latter will secure multi-year Intel Xeon supply capacity, including supply of next-generation Xeon processors codenamed Diamond Rapids, and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for multi-chiplet data center solutions developed in-house.

The EMIB agreement is arguably the biggest news. Microsoft is the first organization to publicly commit to Intel's advanced packaging technology for its own silicon (i.e., it does not mean that Microsoft is the first third party to use EMIB; it is the first party to confirm usage of EMIB), which represents a significant commercial development for Intel Foundry in terms of publicity. However, the announcement does not identify the processors involved, their manufacturing process, production volumes, or deployment schedule. Microsoft was the first company to commit to use Intel's 18A for its data center silicon in 2024, though it is unclear whether the newly declared EMIB packaging agreement relates to the same solution or not. As the majority of high-end data center solutions tend to use multi-chiplet design, it is reasonable to expect Microsoft's future solutions for data centers to use EMIB for multi-die processors.

"Through use of our advanced packaging capabilities with EMIB to scale future generations of Azure infrastructure, Intel and Microsoft can combine the flexibility of heterogeneous integration with the manufacturing scale required for the AI era — giving customers fresh levels of performance and economics when interacting with Azure," said Naga Chandrasekaran, EVP, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

The Xeon agreement provides Intel with greater visibility into future server CPU demand. Importantly, Microsoft has committed to using Intel's next-generation Xeon 'Diamond Rapids,' although the announcement does not disclose purchase volumes or financial terms.

The collaboration extends beyond processor procurement and EMIB. Specifically, Intel and Microsoft are jointly developing infrastructure capabilities that encompass processor architecture, heterogeneous integration, CXL memory expansion, QuickAssist Technology (QAT) acceleration, and Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) security.

  • Sources indicate that A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov.
  • Industry observers note that the 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut.

Sources indicate that A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week.

Industry observers note that the 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV).

China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date.

Recent findings suggest that CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time.

Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

Sources indicate that one of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having released on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions.

China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and debuted its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews.

Recent findings suggest that shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

Latest Update: What it takes to pivot

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There comes a time when many companies need to pivot.
  • In a recent development, there comes a time when many companies need to pivot.
  • From first-hand experience, I can tell you that how you approach a pivot’s first 90 days can make or break your business.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There comes a time when many companies need to pivot. Maybe you want to expand out of your core category into a new one, or maybe you’re making a complete 180. When I joined You.com as COO in January this year, we decided to pivot by consolidating our product and business units around one core offering. Frankly, that offering had always been the heart of the tech giant. This decision came down to evaluating three dimensions of the business: people, products, and customers. From first-hand experience, I can tell you that how you approach a pivot’s first 90 days can make or break your business. When done ineffectively, it can leave employees and customers uncertain. When done well, you can bring both of those groups on board, united under a new vision. Here are three tips for how to have a successful company pivot, from someone who recently navigated it. 1. ARRIVE WITH A THESIS, THEN TRY TO BREAK IT Whether you’re coming into a company for the first time like I did, or you’re a long-time team member, you should always be evaluating its strengths and weaknesses to inform the best next steps to take. I wasn’t trying to shake things up for the sake of change. Rather, I had a series of conversations with the founder and CEO before I even stepped foot in the door that shaped my initial vision and plan for the company’s future. I developed an initial thesis for how the company should move forward. But rather than immediately implementing my ideas, I used the first 30 days to test it, finding its gaps and strengths. When exploring a pivot, keep an open mind and gauge buy-in before making any major changes. I spent my first 30 days diving into the people, product, and customers. I took dozens of one-on-one meetings with employees from all departments and levels, spent enough hands-on time with the products to understand them, and also spoke with dozens of customers about what they liked about the products or how they would change them. I looked at the company the way an investor would from the outside. I asked questions like: Where are we best positioned to win short-term and long-term? Where do we have true competitive advantage? Where is the best market opportunity? Where are our best win rates? Where is our biggest pipeline? Where is our best retention? Even if these answers differ from your original ideas, ego can’t change the data. These efforts validated my initial thesis and gave me the data and examples to commit to the pivot. 2. PIVOT AROUND A NORTH STAR Teams are much more receptive in a return to the mission or reinforcement of the mission rather than a reinvention. You want to frame your pivot around a central anchor point, informed by the data. Another way to think of it is to clarify your North Star and pinpoint the business’s strengths and barriers to success. At You.com, we had success because like most companies, we made things that customers were willing to pay for. We also went out of our way to find solutions to specific problems they were facing. This is all positive, and in the process we made good products. The reality was we sometimes built custom solutions for different customers which were valuable but not scalable. That’s not to say we shouldn’t have pursued it. Companies should branch out, test new ideas, and find creative solutions to new problems. Throughout this process, though, the outcome needs to serve the business’s North Star and value-creation objectives. In our case, a pivot wasn’t completely revamping the product or service. Rather, we realized that the web search API product line was our foundation, and contributed to the majority of our revenues. However, it was not getting the majority of resources. We made the informed decision to reorient our company around this core product and went all-in. This pivot essentially brought us home. When the company introduced in 2021, we were the first to introduce LLMs in a search engine context. A year later, we were the first to connect an LLM to the web and started building the foundation for how AI uses the internet. From this, we developed easier ways for businesses to plug their AI into the web. Over time, we added different layers and custom-built different capabilities. But the pivot was to remove the layers and focus on the foundation. If you’re facing a similar decision, go back to the people, product, and customer. If what’s working is 90% of the business, make it 100% of the business. If the energy comes from removal, and you give it an earnest shot to build the one thing you know you’re good at, watch what happens to the entire organization. 3. CREATE A SOFT LANDING FOR WHAT GETS LEFT It’s important not to trivialize the 10% that gets removed, because those customers bought from us for a specific reason. Telling those customers we were moving on was delicate. Those relationships took years to build and I wanted them to feel honored on the way out. Just like you found creative solutions to their original problems, continue to do that now. In our case, we spun out a joint venture with a professional services partner who could continue supporting businesses with custom-built solutions. Those customers had somewhere to go and didn’t get abandoned. And we could focus all the company resources around a core product. Ninety days of listening and designing bought the next 90 days of full-speed work. People become aligned because you listened. The product is there because it’s what you are excited about and what you do best. The customer trusts you because you demonstrated them focus, authenticity, and caring. Alex Triplett is COO of You.com.

I wasn’t trying to shake things up for the sake of change. Rather, I had a series of conversations with the founder and CEO before I even stepped foot in the door that shaped my initial vision and blueprint for the company’s future. I developed an initial thesis for how the company should move forward. But rather than immediately implementing my ideas, I used the first 30 days to test it, finding its gaps and strengths. When exploring a pivot, keep an open mind and gauge buy-in before making any major changes.

In a recent development, I spent my first 30 days diving into the people, product, and customers. I took dozens of one-on-one meetings with employees from all departments and levels, spent enough hands-on time with the products to understand them, and also spoke with dozens of customers about what they liked about the products or how they would change them.

Recent findings suggest that I looked at the company the way an investor would from the outside. I asked questions like: Where are we best positioned to win short-term and long-term? Where do we have true competitive advantage? Where is the best market opportunity? Where are our best win rates? Where is our biggest pipeline? Where is our best retention? Even if these answers differ from your original ideas, ego can’t change the data. These efforts validated my initial thesis and gave me the data and examples to commit to the pivot.

In a recent development, teams are much more receptive in a return to the mission or reinforcement of the mission rather than a reinvention. You want to frame your pivot around a central anchor point, informed by the data. Another way to think of it is to clarify your North Star and pinpoint the business’s strengths and barriers to success.

It has been revealed that at You.com, we had success because like most companies, we made things that customers were willing to pay for. We also went out of our way to find solutions to specific problems they were facing. This is all positive, and in the process we made good products.

The reality was we sometimes built custom solutions for different customers which were valuable but not scalable. That’s not to say we shouldn’t have pursued it. Companies should branch out, test new ideas, and find creative solutions to new problems. Throughout this process, though, the outcome needs to serve the business’s North Star and value-creation objectives.

In our case, a pivot wasn’t completely revamping the product or service. Rather, we realized that the web search API product line was our foundation, and contributed to the majority of our revenues. However, it was not getting the majority of resources. We made the informed decision to reorient our company around this core product and went all-in.

It has been revealed that this pivot essentially brought us home. When the company launched in 2021, we were the first to introduce LLMs in a search engine context. A year later, we were the first to connect an LLM to the web and started building the foundation for how AI uses the internet. From this, we developed easier ways for businesses to plug their AI into the web. Over time, we added different layers and custom-built different capabilities. But the pivot was to remove the layers and focus on the foundation.

If you’re facing a similar decision, go back to the people, product, and customer. If what’s working is 90% of the business, make it 100% of the business. If the energy comes from removal, and you give it an earnest shot to build the one thing you know you’re good at, watch what happens to the entire organization.

It has been revealed that it’s key not to trivialize the 10% that gets removed, because those customers bought from us for a specific reason. Telling those customers we were moving on was delicate. Those relationships took years to build and I wanted them to feel honored on the way out.

Sources indicate that just like you found creative solutions to their original problems, continue to do that now. In our case, we spun out a joint venture with a professional services partner who could continue supporting businesses with custom-built solutions. Those customers had somewhere to go and didn’t get abandoned. And we could focus all the company resources around a core product.

In a recent development, ninety days of listening and designing bought the next 90 days of full-speed work. People become aligned because you listened. The product is there because it’s what you are excited about and what you do best. The customer trusts you because you demonstrated them focus, authenticity, and caring.

Alex Triplett is COO of You.com.
