M&A Isn’t Just for Significant Companies. Here’s How Startups Can Do It With No Cash.

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1247 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Entrepreneur

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • Most startups are so focused on building stand-alone businesses through traditional sales and marketing that they overlook other ways to grow, such as mergers and acquisitions (M&A).
  • This article will provide a high-level tutorial on what M&A is, why you should consider it, and how to negotiate deals that can get to the finish line, even if you are not large enough to be bankable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Most startups are so focused on building stand-alone businesses through traditional sales and marketing that they overlook other ways to grow, such as mergers and acquisitions (M&A). They simply have not been trained on the topic and don’t know that, for some businesses, it can be a faster, more effective way to scale.

This article will provide a high-level tutorial on what M&A is, why you should consider it, and how to negotiate deals that can get to the finish line, even if you are not large enough to be bankable.

A merger is a combination of the shareholders of two businesses into one. A merger typically involves combining the management teams and operations into one. An acquisition is exactly what it sounds like: your business is acquiring a organization (or being acquired by one), with the acquiring team retaining 100% control over all key decisions in the fresh company. The acquired company’s operations will be integrated into the new company, however the acquiring company sees fit, as the buying company will control all decisions post-transaction. So, you will need to decide which scenario will work best for your needs.

Recent findings suggest that M&A has many advantages, the key ones being speed, economies of scale and removing competition. Since the acquired business is already up and running and, hopefully, producing cash flow, it offers a much faster path to growth. For example, if a restaurant chain was trying to grow from 1 to 2 locations, it would take them over a year to find a site and build it out. But through M&A, that second location is already built and is immediately generating revenues today.

According to recent reports, furthermore, when you combine two businesses, you can eliminate duplicative costs and achieve economies of scale. For example, you don’t need two executive teams, two insurance policies, two marketing agencies, two accounting firms, etc. By removing these duplicative costs, the combined business will end up with a more profitable bottom-line margin, where hopefully 1+1=3.

As for the competitive advantages, by buying a competitor in the market, that will increase your market share and have you competing against one less competitor (which may help your pricing). As an example, in my hometown of Cary, NC, one entrepreneur acquired and rolled up around 20 competing Mexican restaurants, with the goal of ensuring that no matter which Mexican restaurant you ate at, he was getting the sale, with nearly 100% market share.

That all said, things can go wrong with M&A. Be sure to read my prior article on the potential pitfalls with M&A, so you don’t get into any trouble here, and you go into this M&A direction “eyes wide open” to prepare for potential hurdles that may arise in the future.

Industry observers note that depending on the size of the transaction, M&A can be funded either from the buyer’s cash account, or by raising additional capital from investors, or with no cash at all via an exchange of equity between the two businesses. Since most start-ups don’t generate much profit, it is unlikely they will be bankable. So, this last path of exchanging equity makes it possible for companies of any size to pursue M&A without any financing required at all.

The key thing about M&A is that it does not necessarily need to be dependent on economic or financial market conditions. Even if third-party investors have paused new investments during a down market, nothing prevents two businesses from merging in a cashless transaction at any time. So, if you can’t raise capital for your stand-alone restaurant chain growth, you can still be growing using M&A as the driver of that growth.

In a recent development, for established businesses generating revenue and profits, it is pretty easy to value those companies using historical revenue or profit multiples from past transactions in your industry. For example, if most small restaurants are sold at 3x EBITDA, it is reasonable to assume your small restaurant can be valued at 3x EBITDA. A good business broker can advise you on what the normal multipliers will be for the size of your company’s revenues, profits, and growth rate.

It has been revealed that if you don’t have revenues or profits to value, then you need to use another metric. Maybe that is cash invested in the business, or asset value, or the assets themselves. For example, if one real estate owner has 4 locations and another real estate owner has 2 locations, then perhaps those two businesses could be combined into one business where the 4-location business owned 67% and the 2-location business owned 33% of the new company.

According to recent reports, let’s say two self-storage businesses are exploring a merger. One does $6MM in revenue, $1MM in profit, and has 300,000 square feet of buildings (all mature, open for many years). The other has $2MM in revenue, $0 in profit today (but will end up at $1MM after they fully rent out their space) and also has 300,000 square feet of buildings (but they are brand newly introduced still ramping up clients and revenues).

How do you value this? On revenues, it would be 80/20. On profits, it would be 100/0, and on square footage it would be 50/50. If I were the buyer, I would start the ownership at 75/25, and if the smaller business successfully increases its client base per its proposal, it can earn its way up to 50/50 through an earn-out. That seems to be the fairest for all parties; that should get both parties to the finish line.

I am a former investment banker on Wall Street, and M&A is incorporated into my DNA. It is something I am comfortable with, as I have bought and sold many companies over my entrepreneurial career. But if you are a first-timer here, I know it can be “scary.”  But it doesn’t need to be. Surround yourself with smart M&A advisors who have “been there and done that,” both in terms of negotiating M&A and integrating companies post M&A, and everything should turn out just fine.

Recent findings suggest that and hopefully your shareholders will thank you for materially accelerating your growth and helping them to expand their valuation multipliers as a bigger organization. Good luck!

Latest Update: GTA 6’s Best Song Is A Nelly Furtado Cover From Azerbaijan

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones.
  • One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones.
  • One of the radio stations you'll find in the game is Kaleidoscope FM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones. As a music-discovery vehicle, GTA: Vice City introduced me to many '80s classics across a variety of genres. With GTA 6 taking players to Leonida, in which Vice City is located, it's apt that the game features music that many probably would never hear anywhere else. One of the radio stations you'll find in the game is Kaleidoscope FM. It features covers of very-well-known songs that are performed by artists from around the world. It's a fantastic hook for a radio station and delivers some of the catchiest and most-unexpected covers from artists that have a pretty low profile outside of their home countries. The first song I heard on the station, and the one that remains my absolute favorite, is a cover of Nelly Furtado's "Say It Right" from Azerbaijani artists Alim Qasimov and Farghana Qasimova. The duo are known for performing Mugham, a type of music that blends poetry, melody, and improvisation. I had never heard of them before playing GTA 6, but the music instantly transported me to my youth listening to Qawwali, a type of music that is rooted in Islamic sufism. Initially, my exposure to Qawwali, a type of music that is over 600 years old, was limited to my own home, but it has since gained a worldwide following thanks to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, who is known as the King of Kings of Qawwali. These days it's pretty common to hear songs that either sample or are inspired by Qawwali, but, even so, hearing Mugham in GTA 6 was a huge surprise. I didn't expect to be playing Rockstar's latest opus and be reminded of Qawwali. https://www.youtube.com/watch?is=GsirJ2mQmdOdZt1a&v=6iA9fogYpLA I already love "Say It Right"--I think it's one of Furtado and producers Timbaland and Danja's best--but this cover draws out the melancholic soul that underpins the original, giving it a more emotional weight. Much of that can be attributed to the religious mysticism that both Mugham and Qawwali evoke. What I appreciate about this cover is how brilliantly it allows the unfamiliar to grasp what makes Mugham and Qawwali so beautiful by presenting it through a song that many people already have some familiarity with. Both types of music are performed by an ensemble, but the improvisational nature means that others are encouraged to contribute. The use of the kamancheh, tar, and daf, along with the vocals covering Furtado's chorus and the khananda's additions, come together to make the cover feel magical. There are other songs that will no doubt catch you by surprise on Kaleidoscope FM--another favourite is a South Asian cover of "Careless Whisper." Naturally, I was intrigued by how this station came to be and, according to Ivan Pavlovich, Rockstar's vice president of music, it stems from an obsession that studio co-founder Sam Houser has. “Historically, we have always loved to champion a quirky, concept-driven station," Pavlovich told GameSpot. "Sam loves foreign-language covers of his favorite songs and thought this could be that station for GTA VI. Tracking down rights holders proved particularly tricky in certain countries." The biggest surprise, however, is the radio station's host: Academy Award winner Jeremy Irons. "Jeremy Irons has the perfect voice as the travel-weathered host telling tall tales of his adventures from around the world," Pavlovich added. "Jeremy loved the script, and nailed the wry humor of his character in one session. Hopefully, this station makes fans smile as much as we did when we were making it." Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are available now. GameSpot gave it a 10/10, saying that it sets the standard for open worlds impossibly high.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K.
  • Sources indicate that alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips.
  • However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated.

Sources indicate that alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.

However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.

As a result, the firm frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source.

According to recent reports, still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot, its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity.

This trade-off has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.

In a LinkedIn post, Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”.

  • Recent findings suggest that parts of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, normally one of the driest places on Earth, turned red-purple, green, and white in austral spring 2026 following an unusually wet winter.
  • The rains came as El Niño was strengthening in the tropical Pacific.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winter precipitation helped wake dormant seeds in northern Chile, carpeting the desert with what may be the region’s most extensive flowering of the satellite era.

Recent findings suggest that parts of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, normally one of the driest places on Earth, turned red-purple, green, and white in austral spring 2026 following an unusually wet winter. The rain woke seeds lying dormant in the soil, setting off what scientists say may be the most extensive desierto florido, or “flowering desert,” of the satellite era.

The rains came as El Niño was strengthening in the tropical Pacific. During an El Niño, the subtropical Pacific high that normally keeps the region dry weakens, while a blocking high tends to form in the South Pacific near the tip of South America. Together, these shifts push the Southern Hemisphere storm track equatorward.

Beginning in mid-July, a series of storm fronts fed by an atmospheric river brought one of the heaviest July rain events in decades to a long stretch of Chile, from the Atacama region south to Los Lagos, according to Chile’s national weather service (Dirección Meteorológica de Chile). In August, back-to-back winter storms blanketed parts of the Atacama Desert in rare snow.

The spring blooms that followed are visible in these satellite image pairs, which show the desert at different stages of flowering on September 14 (left) and on October 24 (right). The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 acquired the September images, and the OLI on Landsat 9 acquired the October images.

It has been revealed that the pair above demonstrates a part of the desert about 30 kilometers (20 miles) southwest of Copiapó, near the eastern sector of Desierto Florido National Park. The red-purple areas prominent in the October 24 scene are vast blooms of pata de guanaco, most likely Cistanthe longiscapa or another Cistanthe species, according to Roberto Chávez, a remote sensing scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso.

In a recent development, chávez and colleagues photographed the Cistanthe blooms (above) in the area that same day. They were in the field to study the bloom with satellite data, drones, and digital cameras. The project aims to use these data to map how the bloom’s biodiversity changes across space and over time, to inform land-use planners and conservation managers.

Industry observers note that the pair below shows another part of the blooming desert, about 50 kilometers (30 miles) southwest of Copiapó. It lies within a priority area of the desert cited for its biological significance, including the flowering landscape.

Cistanthe is abundant here in the October view, but the September scene (left) reveals another desert beauty. The green areas capped with white are blooms of suspiros, or Nolana, probably Nolana baccata, according to Andres Moreira-Muñoz, a scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso who studies plant geography. The researchers photographed the Nolana-covered hillsides below on September 24, 2026.

It has been revealed that satellite data have been key to understanding the Atacama’s blooms. A 2014 study used Landsat observations to map where flowering and fog-fed plants grow around the Copiapó dune field. And a 2019 study used NASA’s long-term vegetation record to identify 13 Atacama Desert blooms between 1981 and 2015.

Compared with those past blooms, the 2026 event stands out. “This instance of the ‘blooming desert’ phenomenon appears to be the most significant to date—in terms of its extent, intensity, and duration,” Moreira-Muñoz noted, “at least since we began using remote sensing.”.

NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey. Photos by Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, Chile, acquired during Fondecyt Regular Project 1251184 (ANID, Chile): Spatiotemporal variation of Flowering Desert biodiversity via multispectral remote sensing. Story by Kathryn Hansen.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s a fresh vibe-coded OS in town going by the name of LiberNT.
  • It has been revealed that liberNT has been under development for some time, but on Wednesday it made a big leap.
  • This still fledgling operating system is designed (mostly) for modern hardware and focuses on 64-bit platforms: amd64, arm64 and riscv64.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s a fresh vibe-coded OS in town going by the name of LiberNT. Its name provides a substantial clue to its nature: Liber (free), NT (New Technology architecture, as in Windows NT). As it has been released under GNU’s GPL3.0 license, LiberNT also provides a free new way to run apps designed for Microsoft’s Windows 11.

It has been revealed that liberNT has been under development for some time, but on Wednesday it made a big leap. Reading the intro, you might have wondered if this work had a ReactOS connection, and indeed there is. But what started as a fork of ReactOS has already got a newly introduced boot loader, graphics stack, memory manager – and yesterday a new kernel. “LiberNT is not affiliated with or endorsed by the ReactOS project or Microsoft,” insist the devs behind this OS.

This still fledgling operating system is designed (mostly) for modern hardware and focuses on 64-bit platforms: amd64, arm64 and riscv64. Ambitiously, the goal is to develop this OS to deliver a free Windows alternative that is “stable, reliable and efficient.” On that latter point, yesterday’s blog update relays some impressive efficiency and performance stats.

The LiberNT team has benchmarked their eponymous OS against Microsoft’s Windows NT, and it beats it hands-down in 112 of 132 system tests. The testing assessed performance in the following areas: file caching, memory handling, threads and locks, plus FAT32 and NTFS storage. Interestingly, both the free and commercial OS were benchmarked on a Mac with an Apple M3 Pro chip. We scanned through the results, and the worst loss for LiberNT was a 28% performance deficit vs Win11, but it claims some astounding relative performance wins showing the free OS being over 2000% faster.

In a recent development, the devs are entirely clear about the fact that the operating system was vibe coded. “AI is part of how LiberNT is built. It helps us review and write code, and everything it writes is then reviewed by a human,” explains a section of the GitHub page for the project. “Before anything reaches the main branch, a person runs and validates the end-to-end tests. We care about this project too much to let a regression slip through.”.

If the above highlights about this new OS's scope, mission, compatibility, and performance have whetted your appetite, there is the full code available via the GitHub link (top), and even some ready-made builds as bootable disk images. Indeed, I’m quite eager to give this new OS a spin. Hopefully, it works as well as the ambitious developers suggest, and I won’t be disappointed by any stability challenges using my daily productivity apps like Firefox, Word, and an old release of Photoshop.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto games have regularly kept up with the times, and in GTA 6, you once again have a smartphone that you can use to interact with the world around you. From getting fresh missions to goofing off by wasting some in-game time on social media, the smartphone in GTA 6 is a pretty handy tool for rising up the social--and criminal--ranks of Leonida. It comes equipped with several apps, and while not every one of them is essential, you'll want to keep an eye open for certain notifications. Here's a closer look at what each app does. How to use your smartphone As a quick reminder, you can whip out your smartphone by using the Up key on the D-pad. From there, you can navigate through the apps menu using the directional keys. GTA 6 smartphone apps WAiNK The bread-and-butter app for aspiring car thieves, the WAiNK app can be used to inspect vehicles for any hidden security features. Scanning a car will let you see its estimated value, which security features it has installed, if it's locked, and how much it'll cost to register it under your name. Scooter Bros Need your personal vehicle in a hurry? A call to Scooter Bros will allow you to summon your ride to your location, so long as you don't mind the couriers stashing their little two-wheeled ride in your trunk. Whatup GTA 6's instant messaging app, this will allow you to get scoops and chat to characters, without ever needing to verbally engage with them. It's also useful for getting new missions and tips on how to make some quick cash with side-activities. Camera It's a camera. It can take selfies. What else were you expecting? Gallery Nothing too surprising here, as the Gallery app is used for checking out all the smartphone pictures you took. It also has a few archived pictures, which show off Jason and Lucia's life prior to the events that kicked off the GTA 6 storyline. Fitness Staying in shape is highly recommended in GTA 6, and this fitness app will allow you to track your gains and how your stats are steadily leveling up from all those deadlifting sessions. Snapmatic Do a little doomscrolling on the side with the social media app, which has a feed full of Leonida's citizens posting about their daily lives, as well as plenty of memes and brainrot content. You can even like posts and read the comments attached to them--if you dare. News Leonida is a busy city, and the news app will let you keep track of all the latest developments. Weather How many seasons can you expect in a single day? Check the weather app to find out. Settings It's not too detailed, but the option to change Jason's wallpaper and ringtone in the settings menu is a nice little touch. While the smartphone will be a handy companion, you can also check out our GTA 6 guides hub for even more tips and tricks. It's being constantly updated with new walkthroughs and features, so if you want to check out the full list of GTA 6 radio stations, how to increase your wanted level, and much more, the answers are only a click away.

No more asteroid landing: Engine trouble forces Japan's Hayabusa2 probe to change plans

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters.
  • The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft rolled out back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu.
  • Sources indicate that but Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters.

The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft rolled out back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu. Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune.

Sources indicate that but Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan.

It has been revealed that but Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan.

The spacecraft will instead target 2015 BM510, another tiny asteroid. And there will be no landing: Hayabusa2 is scheduled to make a high-speed flyby of the near-Earth object in April 2028.

Sources indicate that the decision was confirmed at a Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) press conference on Tuesday (Nov. 17), a day after a Cabinet Office space policy subcommittee meeting. The final functioning thruster out of Hayabusa2's four ion engines suffered a malfunction in mid-August, according to JAXA officials, while a sensor detected unexpected erosion of the spacecraft's surface during its long voyage in space.

"The deterioration of the onboard equipment ... is becoming increasingly evident," Japan Times quoted Yuya Mimasu, team leader of the extended mission, as saying.

Despite losing the opportunity to land on KY26, the Hayabusa2 mission has been a huge success for JAXA, and the fresh direction promises its own intrigues. Asteroid 2015 BM510 has already attracted interest; it's the primary target of a proposal for the European Space Agency's mini-Fast mission series. Scientists describe the body as a D-type asteroid, meaning it's thought to be organic-rich and comet-like, and may have originated in the outer solar system.

Around the same time as Hayabusa2 conducts its high-speed flyby in April 2028, JAXA is also scheduled to launch its next asteroid mission, Destiny+. Launching along with ESA's Ramses mission to study Apophis, Destiny+ will first make a flyby of the infamous asteroid ahead of its very close approach to Earth in 2029 before heading to asteroid 3200 Phaethon, the parent body of the Geminid meteor shower.

Nine Korean startups vie for a spot in Disrupt 2027’s Startup Battlefield 200 competition

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

💡 Key Takeaways
  • TechCrunch’s yearly Startup Battlefield 200 competition sees hundreds of companies from across the world trying every year to get a chance to pitch in front of VCs and the international tech community at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference.
  • This week, nine early-stage South Korean startups pitched at DETO 2026, a technology conference in Seoul, to earn a spot in next year’s Startup Battlefield 200.
  • In a recent development, the startups work across the deep tech sector, including healthcare, fintech, energy, semiconductors, and AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TechCrunch’s yearly Startup Battlefield 200 competition sees hundreds of companies from across the world trying every year to get a chance to pitch in front of VCs and the international tech community at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference.

This week, nine early-stage South Korean startups pitched at DETO 2026, a technology conference in Seoul, to earn a spot in next year’s Startup Battlefield 200.

In a recent development, the startups work across the deep tech sector, including healthcare, fintech, energy, semiconductors, and AI. All nine startups are looking to enter the U.S. market as part of the broader international expansion looks.

According to recent reports, voinosis, which develops AI to detect changes in brain health through voice analysis, won the competition. The other eight startups are listed below in alphabetical order.

Industry observers note that voinosis is developing an AI tool that analyzes speech patterns such as pitch, pauses, rhythm, and response times to detect changes linked to brain health. Each voice check takes less than five minutes.

The manufacturer says its technology has been tested in Greek, Japanese, and English, and its product doesn’t require separate training for each language. In a clinical study involving 146 participants, the startup claims its tech achieved 88% accuracy in screening for potential cognitive concerns.

Sources indicate that voinosis targets hospitals, senior living facilities, insurers, and individual consumers. It also plans to link voice checks with cognitive training, assessments, and treatment provided by healthcare professionals.

The startup was founded by Grace Shin, who spent more than 25 years as an otologic surgeon. The startup is currently raising a Series A round and has already secured a South Korean pharmaceutical company as a strategic investor.

Awesome Lab, based in Seoul, makes ThermoFlux, a heating system that uses water electrolysis and ionization to generate heat. The system can manage heat production for buildings, water supply, and industrial processes. The organization claims its technology can reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions.

For its international expansion, Awesome Lab is taking a different approach in each market. In the U.S., it plans to supply core OEM modules and work with boiler, water heater, and HVAC companies on product development.

Crosshub helps travelers and international visitors verify their identities and set up payment methods abroad. Its platform, IDBlock, combines identity verification and payment services using self-sovereign identity (SSI) and zero-knowledge proof.

The firm claims its platform helps owners prove their identity across borders without sharing unnecessary personal information. Crosshub is also integrating this technology with payment systems to improve access to financial services for travelers.

DeepFusion AI has developed a 4D radar-based imaging system with additional sensors for autonomous mobility, robotaxi, maritime surveillance, and defense applications. The system combines RF sensors with radar and lidar to detect objects, movement, or distance without a direct line of sight. All sensors are supposedly packed into a single, customizable unit.

Sources indicate that EFLOW develops special motors that can produce more torque, or rotational force, while taking up less space for use in robots, drones, satellites, and other mobility applications. The startup also develops actuators that control how robotic joints move.

Sources indicate that otiton Medical makes two medical devices: One specializes in measuring body temperature, while another can capture ear canal images and analyze the eardrum. The manufacturer states its AI was trained on about 55,000 images of eardrums, and the device has received medical certification in South Korea.

Riibotics states it can deploy robots into warehouses within a day. Riibotics wants to reduce deployment costs for warehouses by streamlining setup, which includes infrastructure setup, warehouse mapping, system integration through custom middleware, task programming, and safety checks.

Ternell, a semiconductor startup based in Ulsan, is developing a new type of memory to help AI chips use less power.

Unlike conventional two-state memory, Ternell’s T-SRAM system adds a third state for more efficient data storage. Founded in 2019 by KyungRok Kim, a former Samsung Electronics engineer, Ternell reports that tests with 28-nanometer chips showed a 33% to 102% increase in memory capacity per area, and a 55% to 71% reduction in energy needed to access data, compared with conventional SRAM.

Testbank is a Korean edtech startup developing Solve, an app that converts printed study materials, such as workbooks and test-prep books, into interactive digital versions.

According to recent reports, the startup uses AI to identify question and answer spaces in publishers’ PDF files while preserving the original layout. Solve lets you write answers directly on the page and be graded automatically.

#110. Beyond Tokens: Why Intelligence Per Watt Is The Metric That Matters

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1010 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

Beyond Tokens: Why Intelligence Per Watt Is The Metric That Matters

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Steven Woo, fellow and distinguished inventor at Rambus.
  • ​AI progress centers on tokens: tokens processed, tokens generated, tokens per second and tokens per watt.
  • Sources indicate that “Intelligence Per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency Of Local AI,” published in November 2025 by a Stanford team, found that small local models can accurately answer 88.7% of single-turn chat and reasoning queries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Dr. Steven Woo, fellow and distinguished inventor at Rambus.

​AI progress centers on tokens: tokens processed, tokens generated, tokens per second and tokens per watt. And because tokens are easy to count, they’ve become the default unit of AI performance. But token-based metrics are only part of the story and miss what people really want. A more useful metric, and one closer to the industry’s goal, is how much intelligence a system delivers per watt.​.

Sources indicate that “Intelligence Per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency Of Local AI,” published in November 2025 by a Stanford team, found that small local models can accurately answer 88.7% of single-turn chat and reasoning queries. Intelligence efficiency—capability delivered per watt—improved 5.3 times between 2023 and 2025, roughly 3.1 times from better models and 1.7 times from better hardware—factors that compound rather than add. This efficiency, not pure token throughput, will determine how well AI can keep scaling.​​.

Recent findings suggest that ask a CFO, CIO or CTO running AI workloads what worries them, and it’s rarely whether they’re generating enough tokens. Although tokenmaxxing has become a metric that some companies use to measure AI engagement, others see the dangers of simply measuring token consumption independent of productivity and delivered value. Several companies are cutting back on token spending, with Uber among others stating in May 2026 that it had already spent its 2026 AI budget, and their COO adding it was becoming “harder to justify” their internal AI costs. There’s a growing call for valuemaxxing, which directs teams toward measurable outcomes based on the value being generated by these tokens.​.

Concerns about measuring token usage are compounded by the fact that reasoning models don’t produce a single response per query; they work through an internal chain of intermediate tokens the user never sees. Published work on model development puts these generations in the thousands to tens of thousands of tokens. That means a query can consume far more resources than its visible output suggests.​.

The pressure to continuously improve value and reduce the cost per token extends beyond inference bills. TrendForce expected server DRAM contract prices to rise 13% to 18% quarter over quarter in Q3 2026, so memory, one of the critical workhorses for AI processing, is getting more expensive as it’s being asked to do more.​​.

For hardware companies, that changes the questions being asked. It stops being how many tokens a chip can generate and becomes how much bandwidth memory can deliver per dollar and per watt, and how these metrics will improve in the future.​.

For decades, the semiconductor industry relied on Dennard scaling to improve power efficiency. As transistors shrank, they drew less power, so more compute arrived without a matching jump in energy use. That relationship broke down in the mid-2000s as transistors continued to shrink, but the automatic power benefit that used to come with each fresh process node no longer followed.​.

With this lever gone, the industry had to substitute architectural changes for what used to be a by-product of process scaling. Memory is where much of that effort is going: Moving data is a major consumer of system power, making it one of the largest levers to pull.​.

The case for stacking DRAM directly on top of a processor has been argued for years. The energy needed to move a bit scales with distance. A DRAM stack beside a processor sits 10 to 12 millimeters away. But stacking the DRAM on top of a processor cuts the distance to about a millimeter. Bandwidth improves separately: Memory beside the processor feeds data through the die’s edges, so interconnect scales with perimeter; stacking can move data through the whole face of a die, allowing bandwidth to scale with area.​.

Stacking DRAM has become a focus topic of the semiconductor industry. At Hot Chips 2026, Samsung released more details about zHBM, which places the processor beneath the DRAM stack and claims roughly 70% lower I/O power than the previous generation. That’s what more bandwidth per dollar and per watt looks like.​.

Stacking has manufacturing and engineering challenges. Although silicon conducts heat reasonably well, a stack of DRAM sitting on a hot processor acts like a blanket and prevents heat from being moved away. Samsung’s answer is thinner dies and smaller four-high stacks rather than the 12-high or 16-high configurations conventional HBM supports. The energy saved on data movement is coupled with less thermal resistance to achieve a high performance, thermally viable architecture.​.

Sources indicate that the same constraint is reshaping infrastructure above the die. Enterprise racks that once drew 20 to 30 kilowatts are heading toward hundreds of kilowatts, and eventually toward a megawatt. Power Electronics Magazine reported in January 2026 that 54 volt in-rack distribution “isn’t designed to support the megawatt-scale racks,” and that the transition to 800 volt DC begins in 2027. Copper is expensive and limits current, so when power demand climbs, voltage is the remaining variable that can rise.​.

Delivering the most intelligence for a given dollar and a given watt used to be determined by two scaling trends running together: Moore’s law delivered more transistors per dollar, and Dennard scaling delivered them at lower power. Moore’s law continues, albeit at a slower pace. Dennard scaling doesn’t, so the power portion of that result now has to be engineered deliberately, architecture by architecture.​.

Sources indicate that the industry has hit walls like this before, and the solution was rarely a single breakthrough. It was a return to fundamentals: measuring the right thing and re-architecting around the real constraint instead of the metric that’s easiest to report.​.

Industry observers note that for the CFOs, CIOs and CTOs approving AI budgets, and for the hardware and software teams underneath them, the number worth tracking isn’t simply how many tokens a system produces. It’s how much usable intelligence and value these tokens return for the dollars and the watts spent producing them.

According to recent reports, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Update Thursday, 12:35 p.m. Shares of Anthropic, PBC opened at $111.50 on Thursday in the year’s most hyped stock market debut. That’s roughly 34% higher than the $83 share price set before trading began—itself an increase over the AI giant’s original target range. However, the stock swiftly began to fall in the first hour and was trading at around $99 a share as of this writing. Much of the market also moved lower, with the Nasdaq down around 0.73% as of 12:40 p.m. ET. Original story: Today, the most hyped IPO of the year (and that’s saying something) is expected to finally take place. Claude LLM maker Anthropic, PBC (Nasdaq: ANT) will debut on the Nasdaq to much fanfare and lofty expectations. But while the Nasdaq opens at 9:30 a.m. ET, it’s likely Anthropic’s shares will not begin trading to the general public until later. Here’s what you need to know. The largest IPO in history Today is Anthropic’s market debut, and its shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The initial public offering is the largest in history, surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO in June. The AI giant raised $81.3 billion in the offering. The forthcoming stock listing is also the most-hyped of the year. As Fast Firm previously noted, Anthropic is considered a pure-play AI company. That is, the company’s sole business is artificial intelligence, as opposed to, say, SpaceX, which is mainly a space transportation and telecommunications company first, and an AI company second. As the largest pure-play AI IPO ever, there’s a lot riding on how the shares react. If investors scoop them up and the share price pops, it could suggest that Wall Street still has an appetite for riskier AI-related stocks, despite recent pullbacks in the broader tech market. However, don’t expect to know how ANT shares are performing as soon as the Nasdaq opens at 9:30 a.m. ET. That’s because, despite the market open, the first buy and sell orders for ANT shares likely won’t be fulfilled until later in the day. What time do Anthropic’s shares begin trading today? If a stock is already listed on an exchange, its shares usually begin trading to the public as soon as that exchange opens. But for market debuts, things are a little different. Stock exchanges know that there is frequently a flurry of orders (both buy and sell) when a hot stock debuts. If the stock were to trade immediately when the market opened, it could cause extreme price volatility, sending the stock up or down significantly in a matter of seconds. Another reason is operational: Nasdaq simply needs time to match orders—buyers with sellers—and determine a price. Because of this, markets like the Nasdaq have procedures in place that delay trading by a little bit so buyers and sellers can get a better idea of demand and price the stock accordingly. Nasdaq calls this a Halt Cross. Only once Nasdaq has determined an opening clearing price based on all its buy and sell orders does it release the stock for trading. Why does this sound familiar? If this sounds familiar, it’s because it’s exactly the same process that happened with the SpaceX IPO. While SPCX shares debuted on the Nasdaq on June 12, they did not begin trading immediately when the Nasdaq opened at 9:30 a.m. ET. Instead, SpaceX’s shares began trading about two to three hours after the morning bell. So, what time, then, will Anthropic’s shares actually begin trading on the Nasdaq? It’s impossible to say for sure. Nasdaq’s rules don’t restrict the Halt Cross to a certain defined period, such as two hours. The Halt Cross lasts as long as it needs to. However, if history is any indication, the Halt Cross usually ends anywhere from 2-4 hours after markets open. That rough estimate suggests that Anthropic shares will begin trading at some point roughly between 11:30 a.m. ET and 1:30 p.m. ET today.

Sources indicate that newly introduced arrivals are landing in the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog this month, but at the same time, you can also expect a few departures from that gaming library. Fortunately, the number of games leaving soon are on the smaller side, as there'll be only three exits in total. Unfortunately, one of those games that you're running out of time to play through the Game Catalog is a massive and pretty fun fantasy title, so get those hours in while you can. PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving soon Granblue Fantasy Relink Granblue Fantasy Relink Somerville Fade to Silence This month's biggest departure is Granblue Fantasy Relink, a massive fantasy game with a storybook art style, cinematic boss fights, and a large roster of characters who all possess unique abilities to master. First released in February 2024, Granblue Fantasy Relink is built around real-time combat and flashy team-up mechanics, making for a visually striking experience overall. While the story isn't much to write home about, it's the gameplay and worldbuilding where this Granblue spin-off shines, and it got even better earlier this year with the Endless Ragnarok expansion. In comparison, Somerville is a story-rich puzzle game that's oozing atmosphere with its slick art direction, and Fade to Silence is a single-player and co-op survival-crafting adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world that is feeling the chill of an eternal winter. While the Game Catalog is going to be a little poorer without those three titles, it is getting some great games this month. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach is the headline act, and it'll be joined by several more titles like Atomfall, Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake, and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii. All PlayStation Plus subscribers can also grab a trio of freebies between now and November 30: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered, and Monster Train 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in the early 2000s I (Bing) found myself crouched in an office cubicle frantically scribbling down a few things I thought the video game industry could teach a burgeoning online bookstore. I was initially reluctant when my friend, the legendary venture capitalist John Doerr, asked me to take a meeting in Seattle with a buzzy, young startup CEO. I was a midcareer video game executive and this particular founder had already been named Time’s 1999 person of the year. Terrified to look a fool, I ducked into a cubicle at the Electronic Arts office in Seattle and outlined an idea for an online customer loyalty program based on the strategy that had turned Madden NFL into a forever franchise by giving gamers reasons to come back year after year. I practically stuffed the one-pager in Jeff Bezos’s hand the first time we met over coffee. He laughed, but indulged me and unfurled the page. I started my career in video games as a marketing chief, and I was still in the habit of writing headline copy for all my one-pagers. Across the top of this one I wrote: Amazon Prime. Jeff would say that Prime’s success was a good surprise, but when you know video games, when you understand the magical ways that they tap into our intrinsic motivations and make us want to come back again and again, you understand that game design thinking has the potential to increase retention and engagement in almost any walk of life. After Amazon Prime worked so well, I brought the lessons of video games to all kinds of consumer industries, from entertainment products like Spotify to financial products like Better Mortgage to educational products like Coursera and Duolingo and even weight loss apps like My Fitness Pal. A bad rap I used to call the craft of applying video game design to consumer products “video gamification,” but these days gamification has a bad rap. Some of the smartest business minds I know brush it off as a short-lived 2010s trend that didn’t pan out. I’ve heard countless product teams complain that the points and leaderboard systems they build into their user interfaces didn’t make a dent in any of their retention metrics. Worse still, I have friends and peers who recoil when they hear the word “gamify,” immediately assuming someone is trying to manipulate their time and attention. Gamification has taken on such a negative connotation that I’ve stopped using the word altogether. The thing is, the so-called “gamification” trend that failed hard in the 2010s was based on a fundamental misunderstanding of what makes successful games work. Product teams that couldn’t figure out how to boost traffic to their app would probably be surprised to learn that successful games rarely rely on competition to motivate players. In fact, in video games, cooperation is a far more crucial mechanism than competition. Connection, mastery, productivity If you’re going to channel the motivational magic of a great game, you need to understand what actually goes into crafting one. The top reasons that players come back to a game are, in order of importance, social connection, personal mastery, and productivity. Most business execs I meet assume that productivity measures like money and rankings are the most important motivational forces, but the video game industry has found for decades that social relationships and the satisfaction of self-improvement far outweigh them. In the early days of the Facebook juggernaut game Farmville, its developer, Zynga, found that the notifications that invited friends to play cooperatively garnered 30 times the clicks that the competitive, brag-based notifications did. In games, a two-way social interaction is the top predictor of whether or not somebody comes back tomorrow. Nongamers find this surprising, but they shouldn’t! We’re human beings, ever motivated to build communities and deepen our relationships with one another. We come back to the games and products that best align with that. One of the great social features of the business networking platform Linkedin is “Endorsements,” where consumers are invited to publicly vouch for their peers and strengthen their professional relationships. Cooperative features like this give people a reason to return to the résumé sharing platform regularly, even when they aren’t searching for jobs. Personal mastery and self-improvement are also intrinsic motivators to every gamer. Mechanics that give people a framework to measure and track self-improvement, like experience points and level-ups, create an invigorating sense of progress with each session. Scores are important in games, but more so as a way to rate individual progression instead of rank it against others. Productivity measures like time saved and money earned also motivate us, especially when they’re paired with our social and mastery priorities. We like earning money, sure, but we love earning money doing things we already wanted to do, and we might forgo it when it comes in direct conflict with our social relationships and sense of self-worth. More of what they want Amazon Prime works because it gives its customers more of what they already want. Free and fast shipping offers an incredible productivity proposition, especially in terms of time saved, and individualized customer profiles help us form identities around ourselves as consumers. Amazon knows that one of the biggest predictors of whether a Prime user renews is how often they use their subscription benefits, but pushing members to make purchases they otherwise wouldn’t risks undermining long-term loyalty. So Amazon treats Prime like a forever game franchise, continually improving the experience and layering on latest benefits like Prime Video, Amazon Music, and prescription savings. Each gives members another reason to use their subscription in ways that already align with their interests. When I gut check a user experience to see if it’s aligned with my own wants and needs, it’s usually as simple as asking, does this product like me? Do I feel better about myself at the end of my session than I did at the beginning? If the answer is no, it usually means the designers are trying to gamify me against my own best interest, like a credit card rewards program that persuades me to spend more money than I would otherwise, or a social media platform that delivers empty dopamine hits without any meaningful upside to my social relationships. These days, I’ve dropped the term “gamification,” but my belief in applying game thinking to products hasn’t wavered. Start with what people actually want, and build around those priorities. You’ll tap into intrinsic motivations far more powerful than any user interface trick or attention hack. That’s real video gamification, and that will always work.

Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives owners access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.
  • Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to get access to better photos.
  • The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives owners access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.

Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to get access to better photos.

The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.

The duo saw a gap in the editing tools on the market and believed that although editing tools can be powerful for enhancing photos, they aren’t very effective at fixing a photo that wasn’t captured well in the first place. Phota Labs changes that by focusing on fixing the shot itself while preserving the natural appearances of those in the image.

According to recent reports, “Phota is your personal photo assistant that can make great photos for any moment you want to keep before you even ask, which means that it’s a very proactive experience,” Zhang told TechCrunch in an interview. “Think of it almost like a photographer or virtual photographer who looks over your camera roll and tries to understand what’s happening and how they could have taken that photo for you on the spot for that scene.”.

The idea is to use AI to transform photos, whether that’s turning a wide-angle group photo into a tighter portrait or transforming a selfie into a regular shot.

Consumers can choose from different photography styles that determine how AI transforms their images, ranging from subtle edits that preserve the original lens and composition to more dramatic transformations that introduce effects like fish-eye lenses, alternative angles, and entirely different perspectives.

While some people turn to ChatGPT and other generative AI tools to enhance or edit images, these tools can often alter a person’s appearance, especially when working with blurry photos because they don’t know what that person actually looks like.

Sources indicate that “For Phota, we built our own tech,” Zhang remarked. ”We built this personalization technology that actually learns about people’s identity and is able to preserve them in any transformation we do to a photo.”.

Images edited with Phota Labs feature invisible watermarks that identify them as altered by AI when shared on social platforms.

The startup is initially targeting people who take tons of photos and like to share them on social media, but don’t want to deal with the tedious process of editing photos. Over time, the founders envision a broader audience, from retirees looking to create beautiful photos for their grandchildren to parents who want to share polished family albums with friends and relatives.

It has been revealed that “We have this obsession with authenticity,” Xia remarked. “I think there’s so much value in connecting AI with real moments and making sure those photos are not perfect, in a sense. That’s why we spend a lot of research into understanding personal context, into building this identity model because we want to make sure the photos are authentic. They’re just better photos of the same moment, rather than saying, ‘Oh, this is an AI image’.”.

In a recent development, xia stated beta customers were excited to see better versions of moments they had actually lived and saw the results as photos of real memories rather than AI-generated images. The founders discovered that users were taking more photos because they knew Phota Labs could enhance them later.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re turning something that’s unusable into something that people want to print,” Zhang said. “People who just love photos but never really got into editing can now experience professional quality that could never have been possible. So, I think that meant so much to us. There’s so many cherished moments for photos, and we really want them to be actually meaningful and something that you can remember.”.

In terms of funding, the company raised a $5.6 million seed round led by a16z last year.

In a recent development, phota Labs is launching as a free app to build an initial user base before exploring a freemium model. The startup also aims to launch an Android app in the future.

Supermicro sued by shareholders over claims Nvidia executive’s wife knew about illicit China sales

💡 Key Takeaways
  • More information about the alleged knowledge of chip diversion by a Supermicro executive is being revealed as shareholders’ civil lawsuit against the company progresses.
  • Sources indicate that cenly Chen is married to former Nvidia Executive Vice President of Worldwide Field Operations Jay Puri, who is also described as the manufacturer’s sales chief.
  • Sources say that Puri controlled the AI chip allocations to server manufacturers, including Supermicro, while the lawsuit claims that Chen decided how many Nvidia racks each Supermicro customer could get.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More information about the alleged knowledge of chip diversion by a Supermicro executive is being revealed as shareholders’ civil lawsuit against the company progresses. According to The Telegraph, the investors alleged that there was “no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company’s illicit sales.” Chen, the former Chief Growth Officer at Supermicro and described by a colleague as the company’s sales leader, resigned from her position in April of this year — about a month after the three Supermicro employees, including its co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, were arrested for a $2.5-billion AI GPU smuggling scheme.

Sources indicate that cenly Chen is married to former Nvidia Executive Vice President of Worldwide Field Operations Jay Puri, who is also described as the manufacturer’s sales chief. The Information also called him Jensen Huang’s right-hand man and noted he was the person that Nvidia’s customers turned to if they wanted to buy chips or had other pressing concerns. The shareholders’ accusations and her relationship with Puri have put the former Supermicro executive in the spotlight, especially after Huang’s sudden departure from the AI chipmaker amid a flurry of affairs and smuggling accusations.

Sources say that Puri controlled the AI chip allocations to server manufacturers, including Supermicro, while the lawsuit claims that Chen decided how many Nvidia racks each Supermicro customer could get. A former Supermicro employee was also quoted in the complaint saying that it was “widely known within the Manufacturer that Chen had to leave because she had sent emails requesting that Nvidia release chips with serial numbers associated with the GPUs illegally diverted to customers in China.” This apparently refers to the serial numbers that were moved from real to dummy servers using a hairdryer.

Sources indicate that supermicro has stated multiple times that it has cooperated with the U.S. government regarding the smuggling investigation and that it has not been included in the lawsuit against the three defendants. Furthermore, the organization has denied her involvement regarding Nvidia GPU allocations. “Chen did not manage Supermicro’s relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers,” a Supermicro spokesperson told The Information. They also said that she left voluntarily and that her LinkedIn profile now reads her current position as CEO of ChronoScale, an Nvidia cloud partner based in Silicon Valley. As for Puri, he stepped away from his position at Nvidia in late August, about two months before the Jensen Huang scandal blew up, although he remains as an advisor to the AI chipmaker.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly introduced set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage.
  • The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov.
  • You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage.

The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms.

You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower.

According to recent reports, "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat debuts and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above.

Recent findings suggest that starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger.

Industry observers note that as SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight.

SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight, Starship's 15th to date, which debuted on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico.

In a recent development, that wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights. Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does.

SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the manufacturer managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try.

And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit. The first set was deployed on Flight 14, which introduced on Sept. 28.

Industry observers note that discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

In a recent development, explanation: Today's image could have been a painting. But what do these colors mean? The brightest star, left of the center, is blue Alnitak (the Girdle): a triple star system best known for being the easternmost star in Orion's Belt. The instantly recognizable shape of a dark horse's head at the center is the aptly named Horsehead Nebula. It is about five light-years tall and lies approximately 1,500 light-years away. It is made of dust and gas that obscure the red glow behind it, which is caused by hydrogen gas being ionized by the bright star Sigma Orionis at the top. The orange nebula with dark filaments on the left is the Flame Nebula. Closer to the Horsehead, the blue reflection nebula NGC 2023 is actively forming stars. The data for this "painting" were collected for almost six hours at the Utah Desert Remote Observatories, but the equipment was remotely controlled by the astrophotographer from his home, over 2,000 km away in Illinois.Tomorrow's picture: V-G-R.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the world’s largest energy shock in history and growing climate change concerns this year are reshaping the future of how people will power homes, drive cars and fuel industries, according to an International Energy Agency report released Thursday.The energy crisis, triggered by the Iran war, will “leave lasting marks” on the world’s energy sector, according to the Paris-based IEA, founded after the 1973-74 energy crisis.Energy-hungry nations will prioritize the security and affordability of their electricity, the report remarked. This is a boon for renewable technologies, like solar, and alternative technologies, like nuclear. But it is also reinforcing the case to keep coal as a backup in times of crisis.This is especially true in coal-rich Asia, which went into energy triage when the Iran war cut off the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow passageway where around a fifth of the world’s traded oil typically flows.The report looks “past the current turmoil to explore the range of energy futures that could emerge from today’s upheaval,” said IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol. He said the Iran war “delivered a huge shock to the system” and warned “the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be.”“I don’t see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before,” he said.Annual United Nations climate talks, known as COP31 and hosted in Turkey this year, are in their second and final week. Before these negotiations, the U.N. announced the world is dangerously close to missing its goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.Electrification — the process of powering homes, cars and industries with electricity — and moving away from planet-warming fossil fuels are the two substantial ticket issues at this year’s climate talks.“The future of the energy system and our climate are inextricably intertwined,” said Rachel Cleetus, climate program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists, who is at COP31. Flagship report forecasts energy future The IEA, the world’s leading intergovernmental energy organization with more than 30 member countries, publishes World Energy Outlooks annually.This year’s 560-page plus report analyzes government and private data to project various future scenarios based on whether countries will continue with current policies or drastically change policies in the face of ongoing crises.The world’s energy sector will clearly have a before and after the Iran war, experts said. In March, the IEA coordinated the emergency release of 400 million barrels of crude oil stocks to stabilize global markets.“This crisis has exposed the price of fossil fuel dependence,” said Mohamed Adow, director of Power Shift Africa. “It’s crazy that a conflict thousands of miles away can send energy bills soaring at home.”Conflicts, trade tensions, climate risks and cyberattacks are increasing the number of possible energy futures. The IEA said the “drive to diversify” fuel supplies will reshape the energy trade.The Middle East will still be the world’s largest oil exporter, but nations will likely reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz. The IEA forecasts the amount of oil transiting the strait could go from 20 million barrels per day before the Iran war, to 8.5 million barrels in 2030, and even under 2 million barrels by 2035.While fossil fuels still dominate national energy mixes, the IEA said renewables — led by solar — and nuclear power are the “biggest beneficiaries” of governments trying to grow domestic energy sources. But energy security concerns may lead coal-rich nations to rely on the fossil fuel as a fallback option during times of crisis.“When we look at how energy crises change the world over the long term, governments are only just beginning to get their head around just how much things will change,” said Dave Jones, co-founder of the think tank Ember. Climate talks eye electrification The ongoing talks in Turkey follow a year rattled by the Iran war’s energy shock, as well as several climate-induced disasters.Global warming adds pressure to rising electricity demand. In what the IEA called a “striking milestone,” energy demand for cooling is overtaking energy demand for heating for the first time.India, the world’s most populous nation, will account for more energy demand growth over the next decade than any other country or region. China, already one of the world’s most electrified economies, may see its electrification grow from 32% last year to 43% by 2035 — the highest among any major economy.At COP31, Turkey is pushing for the world to increase the share of electricity in total global energy consumption from roughly 21% today to 35% by 2035.While the preference would be for this to come from renewable energy, U.N. documents on the negotiating table don’t spell this out. That means coal and other fossil fuels could be used, at least initially.“The IEA’s latest report makes clear that the fossil energy crisis unleashed by the US-Israel war on Iran has irrevocably changed the global energy system, adding to the many reasons why countries would benefit from a rapid transition to clean energy and electrification,” said Cleetus, with the Union of Concerned Scientists. The Associated Press’ climate and environmental coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. The AP is solely responsible for all content. Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator discovery and outreach for brands

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nectar, an AI-powered operating system for marketing, is launching a new AI agent designed to take a lot of the manual work out of influencer marketing, from finding the right creators to contacting them, managing partnerships, and tracking results.
  • Founded by sisters Misbah and Farah Uraizee, both former Meta employees, Nectar came out of stealth last year and uses AI agents to help brands manage social media, customer conversations, content moderation, creator partnerships, and competitor research.
  • In a recent development, confirmed Thursday, its newly introduced “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nectar, an AI-powered operating system for marketing, is launching a new AI agent designed to take a lot of the manual work out of influencer marketing, from finding the right creators to contacting them, managing partnerships, and tracking results.

Founded by sisters Misbah and Farah Uraizee, both former Meta employees, Nectar came out of stealth last year and uses AI agents to help brands manage social media, customer conversations, content moderation, creator partnerships, and competitor research.

In a recent development, confirmed Thursday, its newly introduced “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform. Instead of having marketing teams spend weeks scrolling through social media, building spreadsheets, and sending individual DMs, Nectar wants its agent to handle much of that work automatically.

In a recent development, nectar joins other companies introducing agentic AI assistants designed to automate influencer outreach, including Aspire and GRIN. The launch also comes as more brands turn to creators to reach customers. U.S. spending on creator advertising is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau. As companies work with hundreds or even thousands of creators, keeping track of relationships and measuring results can get pretty difficult.

Recent findings suggest that nectar claims its Creator Agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction. The system analyzes videos to understand what creators post about, how their content fits a brand, and whether their previous partnerships are appropriate. It also checks brand safety by reviewing content in context rather than simply searching for specific keywords.

Nectar then creates ranked lists of recommendations and adds latest matches as creators become more popular.

Once it finds a potential match, the agent can draft and send messages in a brand’s voice, create custom landing pages to collect creator information, and help manage contracts, product gifting, and shipping details. It also remembers previous conversations and interactions, so brands can keep track of relationships without relying on spreadsheets.

Recent findings suggest that “Brands can share voice guidelines in any format, and Nectar picks up the rest from their history,” CEO Misbah Uraizee tells TechCrunch. “On top of that sits a set of proprietary guardrails that keep every draft on tone and in context. Nectar understands what is being remarked in a video, reads the tone of the conversation, and knows the difference between a quote post on X and a TikTok comment section. A brand should not sound identical in both, and with Nectar it doesn’t.”.

Another feature looks for personal milestones in creators’ lives, such as an engagement, a fresh baby, or completing a marathon. The agent can then suggest a personalized message or gift, helping brands build relationships that feel less like one-off advertising deals.

Creator Agent is available today globally and covers Instagram creators and TikTokers.

The firm plans to make the agent available through its Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing teams to use it through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, as well as their own custom-built agents.

This past May, Nectar raised a $30 million Series A round led by Menlo Ventures and its Anthology Fund, which is a joint initiative launched with Anthropic.
