In recent days, my inbox and, I’m sure, the inboxes of many a staffer at gaming publications have been flooded with emails from brands trying to capitalize in some way on all the GTA 6 hype. And look, I get it; of course marketers are going to see an opportunity in associating their brands with a pop culture event of this magnitude. Some are calling the release of GTA 6 the return of the monoculture, or maybe its last gasp. And some of what’s happening I think is fine. Zack caught a Panda Express ad earlier today on another site that was clearly designed to create an association in viewers’ minds between the game and the restaurant, even though there is no official collaboration between Rockstar and Panda Express.

I can’t be mad at this. I’ve been seeing this sort of thing my whole life, brands gesturing toward whatever the cultural vibe or flavor of the month is. It’s whatever, it’s fine. But some of the other efforts strike me as a bit more desperate, and a bit more clueless.

Case in point: Today I got an email announcing that Heinz, the ketchup brand, “Drops Real-Life GORGE Ketchup from Vice City.” Apparently inÂ GTA 6, you can see condiments that are styled to look like Heinz products, but the in-game brand is called Gorge. And sure, ifÂ GTAÂ is gonna spoof your product, I think turnabout is fair play and releasing your own real-life version of said product is fine from, like, an ethical standpoint. But it also strikes me as silly.

I think maybe for me the real problem with this effort had to do with some of the text in the associated email, which just made it all feel to me like an effort cooked up by boardroom marketing execs who don’t really know much about GTAÂ at all. For instance, one line in the email read, “Consider it the ultimate loot drop for ketchup-loving gamers.” Ah yes, if there’s one thing the gamers in my life love as much as spending some quality time in GTA, it’s KETCHUP! And also, GTAÂ doesn’t HAVE loot drops! I mean, maybe it should. Maybe the big climactic missions at the end of each chapter should have bosses you kill who have a 2.5-percent chance of dropping a Legendary pistol that does extra damage and freezes enemies in place with ice magic. But it doesn’t.

It has been revealed that anyway, if you want a shot at scoring some real-life Gorge Ketchup (and I know you do!), I guess visit this post on the Heinz Instagram for details. Happy Gorging!

TheÂ GTAÂ games are often story-generating machines. Part of the fun of playing them is getting to talk to your friends later about the wild encounters and experiences you had in-game. An anecdote about one such encounter from Jason Schreier’s review forÂ BloombergÂ seems to be persuading at least a few folks who previously weren’t interested in playing the game into potentially giving it a try.

Industry observers note that it definitely makes for an attention-grabbing opener to the review. The anecdote reads:.

Several hours into Grand Theft Auto VI, I watched a sedan get smashed from behind by a truck. I had been driving around Vice City, a fictionalized re-creation of Miami with such lifelike graphical fidelity that it can be hard to distinguish the video game from real-life footage, and I pulled to a stop when I saw the two vehicles collide. The truck driver scampered off, leaving the victim trapped in his seat as his engine began to catch fire. I ran over and helped him out of the car. He thanked me, reflecting in astonishment that heâd almost died. Then he noticed that the culprit was a delivery truck for Sahara, the Grand Theft Auto parody of Amazon. This was his big break, he declared. He could sue Sahara for millions.

Recent findings suggest that but he needed demonstrable damages. So he took a deep breath, got back in the car, set his own legs on fire and then re-emerged with burns all over his body. He called his lawyer. Then, as an ambulance approached, he turned and asked me to be a witness in exchange for some of his inevitable payout. I thought about pressing a button to blackmail him but ultimately agreed to help, and he sent me a few thousand dollars on BuckMe, the gameâs version of Venmo.

This is the kind of encounter that Rockstar excels at, an event you just stumble upon that seems random but is actually crafted specifically to give the world that feeling of life, randomness, and spontaneity. And I’m sure this is just one of many such events you might come across in your time with the game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since President Donald Trump’s reelection in 2024, Elon Musk has been one of his biggest allies in Silicon Valley.
  • Since President Donald Trump’s reelection in 2024, Elon Musk has been one of his biggest allies in Silicon Valley.
  • But in an interview at this week’s annual DealBook Summit, Musk suddenly sang a different tune.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since President Donald Trump’s reelection in 2024, Elon Musk has been one of his biggest allies in Silicon Valley. The Tesla CEO has served as both Trump’s employee and his friend: He spearheaded the Trump administration’s Department of Government Efficiency, aka DOGE, and wasn’t shy to tell the press that he came to “love” Trump over the course of their work together. But in an interview at this week’s annual DealBook Summit, Musk suddenly sang a different tune. “I’m not MAGA,” Musk mentioned. “I’m not sure what MAGA means, but if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.” Musk may claim not to know the full extent of what “MAGA” means, but in the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election, he was happy to embrace the term. Wearing an infamous black MAGA hat to one of Trump’s rallies at Madison Square Garden, Musk told the crowd that he’s “not just MAGA,” but “dark gothic MAGA.” Now, though, after the country’s historic shift to the left in this month’s midterm elections, Musk is positioning himself as bipartisan. “I think there are positives and negatives in both parties,” he said. Musk’s historic midterm spending Musk’s recent actions make it hard to believe he doesn’t consider himself bound to the Republican Party. Ahead of the midterms, the world’s richest man became the largest individual political donor in U.S. history, giving $446 million to conservative PACs including his own America PAC, which he founded in 2024 to support Trump’s presidential campaign. But according to Musk, that record-breaking spending wasn’t in direct support of Republicans, but in support of a politically balanced Congress. His goal—“which failed, by the way,” Musk joked—was for Republicans to hold 51 seats in the Senate in 2029. “I think we want to have at least one of either the presidency, the House, or the Senate be of the other party,” Musk said. But the blue tsunami proves that Musk’s investment didn’t pay off. He says he feels “pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it.” He added: “Probably, if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.” Musk’s donations included hefty sums in his home base of Texas, where two Republican candidates he backed, Gov. Greg Abbott and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, lost to Democrats Gina Hinojosa and James Talarico, respectively. But Musk is looking on the bright side, saying he believes that Hinojosa “is going to be quite moderate” as governor. “Based on everything I’ve heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with Gina as governor,” he said. “I don’t think she’s a far-left governor.” A blue wave in tech? Musk isn’t the only tech titan to downplay their GOP affiliations in the wake of the midterms. Last week, Palantir CEO Alex Karp claimed the software company’s products are “essentially progressive” despite its contracts with the Trump administration, including creating surveillance technology for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). “I’ve been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far-left environment,” Karp said. “I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir—all of our products are essentially progressive.” Like Musk, Carp said his support of Republicans has been in service of political moderation, not a right-wing takeover. “My giving is equal Democrat, Republican,” Karp said. “I can tell you, without going into things I’m not gonna disclose, I’m very balanced, and everyone in the political arena knows it. And I’ll tell you what—I’m also not the village idiot.”.

#26. You Can Play Grand Theft Auto 6 At 60fps Using This Absurdly Complicated Method

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1225 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

You Can Play Grand Theft Auto 6 At 60fps Using This Absurdly Complicated Method

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1225 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal.
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal.
  • Sources indicate that irrespective of what platform you play on, Grand Theft Auto VI is limited to 30fps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal. You'll struggle to find a better-looking game on the current generation of hardware, but one concession Rockstar had to make to achieve that was limiting its frame rate--a limitation some players are going to absurd lengths to overcome. Irrespective of what platform you play on, Grand Theft Auto VI is limited to 30fps. Doubling that to the more desirable 60fps is something current console hardware just isn't capable of with this level of visual fidelity and simulation, which means you'll have to rely on other methods of frame generation to get there. That's the idea that underpins technology like Veyra: an open-source real-time video enhancer that uses your PC and HDMI 2.1 capture card to bring frame generation to your console. It's a...complicated process. First you'll need a capable capture card (like one of the many from Elgato) that is able to ingest gameplay at 4K over HDMI 2.1. You'll need to connect that to your PC using certified USB-C 3.2 data cable, which needs to plug into a suitable motherboard with True USB 3.2 Gen 2 support. On the pricier end of the requirements, you will need a relatively powerful GPU, with the creators recommending a RTX-40 or newer card from Nvidia in order to tap into the card's Tensor cores (that are used for frame generation on PC). Pair that with an OLED monitor, which is also strongly recommended thanks to its near-instant pixel response times, and you've got everything you need to finally enjoy Grand Theft Auto VI (and more) at higher frame rates. Veyra is able to take gameplay captured on your console and apply a variety of enhancements over the footage, which is ultimately displayed (and played) through the PC you're capturing the footage to. You can utilize upscaling and frame generation techniques from Nvidia, AMD, and Intel to enhance both the resolution and perceived fluidity of your console games this way, with as minimal latency as possible. Given all the parts in the chain, from your console, to the capture card, and through to your PC, escaping any additional latency is impossible. But Verya is seemingly built with mitigating latency as its highest priority, and seems to achieve that based on feedback from some users on Reddit. Is it worth it to go through this much hassle to play GTA 6 at 60fps? If you have all the required hardware then it's at least worth a shot, even just for the sake of curiosity. But actually investing in a setup to achieve this is probably overkill. For starters, it requires a PC that will probably be capable enough to play Rockstar's latest sequel at or on-par with the console version once it does land on PC (which will reportedly be sooner than you think). Capture cards are not outrageously expensive, but they're also not free, which can also be remarked for all the high-quality cables you'll need between each of the three required devices. I admit, I admire the dedication to playing Grand Theft Auto VI at launch in the best possible way, but I would wager that you're likely going to be spending a lot more time troubleshooting some incompatibility somewhere along this chain of dependencies instead of enjoying the game itself. Still, if you're curious you can find a lot of detailed information about what this setup requires and why, and determine for yourself if it's worth the price to cruise around Leonida with a bit more fluidity.

Industry News: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: It revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January.
  • Industry observers note that the manufacturer invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year.
  • But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: It revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both latest investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

Industry observers note that the manufacturer invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it demonstrates how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.

But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.

Nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.”  Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic and OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications.

It’s also become a massive financier of the data center build-out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio.

The firm made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earnings call, Kress noted Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.”.

But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the manufacturer will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm.

According to recent reports, huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with newly introduced investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies.

“We intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this last quarter and going forward,” Kress said on the earnings call on Tuesday. Just how strategic startups will be under her leadership, and under the future permanent CEO, remains to be seen. But for now, VCs are bracing for a meaningful pullback in capital.

In a recent development, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and people are discovering all manner of little details in the game that speak to the developer's commitment to realism. One such detail is the game's weightlifting and general fitness systems, and they seem to be pretty great, so much so that if you're thinking about getting into weight lifting, GTA 6's lessons are a good place to start. For starters, Jason has a home gym, and that's just smart on his part. Not having to leave your house and head to a gym is a godsend for anyone short on time or for those who simply enjoy the solitude of slinging weight around alone. For Jason, it's even better--he lives on the water, and it looks pretty damn serene heading to his workout pad for a sweat. If you're thinking about crafting your own home gym, Jason's setup is exactly what you need to get started: a squat rack, bench, kettlebells, barbells, and iron plates. Garage gym expert Cooper Mitchell also pointed out that Jason's squat stand uses 3"x3" uprights with 1" holes, and that's a great choice by Jason--or you--because it means you have universal support for other attachments from different brands that you might add over time. Jason also has his setup outfitted with horse stall mats, which is another super-smart choice on his part, not only to protect his flooring, but also because they hold up in the outdoor setting that he uses. Having personally invested in horse stall mats for my own home gym, I can vouch for their incredibly sturdy makeup. They are far better than the cheap interlocking styrofoam mats. They cost more and are a massive pain in the ass to get in place due to their weight and structure. But that's just how it is. I am a little concerned about Jason leaving all of this equipment outdoors, considering it rains a lot in Florida and is very humid. This may not be ideal for his iron plates, specifically, or his rack. That being remarked, Jason (and Lucia) can also work out at an indoor gym, so they have their bases covered. Moving beyond the equipment, GTA 6 really nails the details on how to actually build muscle. To maximize your gains, first you need to use proper form. If Jason does not gently lower the bar on chest presses, he fails his reps, and that's basically how it works in real life. Making slow, controlled movements with any free weight is good practice, and it's nice to see the game reinforce this by giving you a fail state when you move the weight too quickly or in an uncontrolled manner. Of course, you can pack on muscle with bad form and so-called "ego-lifting," but it's generally more advisable to focus on your form. Making light weight feel heavy is the real path to gains. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfztIWqrJ7s After hitting chest, doing squats, or swinging the kettlebell, GTA 6 encourages you to eat some protein to lock in your gains, and that's also how it works in real life. You can lift all you want, but if you're not eating enough protein, you won't progress optimally. In GTA 6, your protein intake can come in the form of shakes and bars that Jason has at home, or he can head out into the world and grab a bite that way. You also need to rest to feel your best and see the most improvements to your physique in GTA 6, and that's also good advice in real life. When you're in the act of lifting, you're tearing your muscles apart to make them grow back bigger via hypertrophy, but the actual muscle growth happens during rest and sleep. GTA 6 goes even further with its own dedicated fitness app on your phone that tracks your progress and serves as a reminder to stay, as the kids say, locked in. A word to the wise, though: Do not get too obsessed with tracking your macros and workouts in the game or in your personal life. Life is meant to be lived and enjoyed, even if it means you're not in "optimal" shape. Your health and fitness journey is personal to you. So go eat a donut and drink a beer at the same time like Jason does. You do not need to have 8% body fat like Take-Two's own CEO Strauss Zelnick does. Enjoy your life, in Vice City and out, but if you want some tips on how to get started, GTA 6 offers a solid foundation to build from.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Army is planning to blow up roughly 5 tons of bomb-making materials in Iowa on Friday, a volatile event expected to send a plume of toxic lead dust into the air as far as 90 miles away.
  • Army is planning to blow up roughly 5 tons of bomb-making materials in Iowa on Friday, a volatile event expected to send a plume of toxic lead dust into the air as far as 90 miles away.
  • The unusual event may sound like a side quest straight out of Grand Theft Auto VI, but it holds potentially serious health consequences for people in the area.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the U.S. Army is planning to blow up roughly 5 tons of bomb-making materials in Iowa on Friday, a volatile event expected to send a plume of toxic lead dust into the air as far as 90 miles away. The chemicals are unstable enough that moving them poses a high risk of explosion, a fact that makes a planned detonation the comparatively safe option. The unusual event may sound like a side quest straight out of Grand Theft Auto VI, but it holds potentially serious health consequences for people in the area. The detonation is set to take place at noon Central time at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, a small town in the southeast corner of the state. The Army described the planned explosion’s hazards in an advisory to local residents, noting that the long-stored barrels of unstable lead azide are expected to create elevated levels of airborne lead when detonated. The advisory states that lead levels are expected to remain below the threshold “at which EPA would require protective actions be taken,” but goes on to describe many measures that residents should take to protect themselves during the event. “The detonation will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground,” it continues. “Residents in Middletown will hear a loud noise; feel vibrations from two consecutive, rapid detonations; and see a plume of dust which is expected to linger for no more than one hour after the detonation, depending on wind speed.” The explosion is expected to be large enough that locals close to Middletown City Park and Butterfly Park could experience “localized window damage.” Residents have been asked to leave their houses for six hours on the day of the detonation, as both locations are less than a quarter of a mile from the detonation zone. 2 lead exposure pathways pose serious dangers The Army is also cautioning people who live or work nearby to avoid the area, stay indoors, keep windows closed, and set their heating and cooling units to recirculate air within their homes in order to minimize potential exposure. Schools in communities including Danville and Mediapolis will close Friday to protect students from lead exposure—both airborne dust and settled dust. “Deposition of lead-containing dust may occur after the detonation on surfaces within certain areas affected by the detonation plume,” the Army’s warning states, encouraging residents to wet-clean surfaces exposed to the chemical dust after the explosion takes place. The advisory, which also includes a map predicting the path of the toxic dust, warns that children, pregnant women, and older adults in particular should avoid contact with lead particles. Only about 400 people live in the Iowa town where the blast will take place, but toxic dust is expected to drift into the air and deposit itself 30 miles north in more populated neighboring communities like Morning Sun, Mediapolis, and Wapello. Airborne lead dust could cause problems to people who inhale it as far away as Cedar Rapids, which is 90 miles from the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. Even Illinois, the state next door, is on high alert for the explosion. “There is no safe level of lead in the body, and when inhaled or swallowed, it can pose serious health risks,” Dr. Sameer Vohra, director of the Illinois Department of Public Health, said in a health advisory. “Illinois residents who may be affected by the detonation can stay safe by staying indoors and keeping windows closed for 24 to 48 hours.”.

Given how good the game is on console, the wait will almost certainly be worth it.

Given how good the game is on console, the wait will almost certainly be worth it.

Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here for millions of players who own a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X / S, and those who initiative to buy a console, despite rising costs this year, just to play it. As you have likely already noticed, the launch is inescapable, and that’s especially tough if you’re a PC gamer.

I’m sorry to remind you that the clock has only just now started ticking down to the unannounced yet inevitable release of the PC version. Good luck with avoiding Twitch and browsing the internet while trying to remain oblivious to the violent (and romantic) delights that await you.

In a recent development, seeing Leonida in true 4K at an unlocked frame rate with full ray-tracing effects and extended draw distances, among other graphical improvements, might be a thing you can do on your PC as early as sometime in Q1 2027, if recent reports are accurate. Regardless, early 2027 is not right now. Speaking as someone with a capable gaming desktop, I’m sad to say that FOMO has already gotten the best of me. I bought GTA VI on the PS5 and will probably double-dip and buy it again on PC, just like I did with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2. The psychology of me, a weak-willed consumer, is one that publisher Rockstar Games and really any other organization in its position would be happy to exploit.

Recent findings suggest that the PC version of GTA VI will launch, eventually, in a very different landscape than the PC ports of Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA V did. Despite the recent downturn in PC sales driven by increased RAM prices, there are considerably more players on PC now than there were a decade ago. SteamDB’s charts show that Steam’s concurrent owners alone have more than doubled (from around 20 million to over 40 million now) since 2020.

A chunk of those people are likely made up of console expats who decided to migrate to PC for various reasons. Some wanted to experience the fun of building their own desktop, while some were mainly convinced by the fact that you can get more power for your money with a PC than with a PlayStation 5 Pro or Xbox Series X. For a subset of people, the convenience of getting something like a Steam Deck to bring your PC game library with you anywhere more than makes up for its lack of power. There are many other justifiable reasons for making PC your main gaming platform, like getting faster access to discounts on digital games, not paying for online multiplayer, ultrawide monitor resolutions, being able to buy games from one of several platforms, and having one device that you can use for work and play.

Rockstar seems poised to deliver the definitive version of GTA VI on PC on its own terms, and I’m interested to see what the end result will be. In addition to building the best-looking version of the game made to run well across countless configurations, its PC optimization efforts are likely also more focused than before on ensuring decent performance on lower-end hardware (including PC handhelds). With a 200-plus-gigabyte install size on consoles, I dread how substantial it’ll be on PC.

Recent findings suggest that ideally, the PC version will launch alongside an improved version of GTA Online (whether it’s free to play is anyone’s guess), and maybe with upgraded GTA roleplay tech to support it. I’m hopeful that the PC version of GTA VI will come in early 2027, but if the numerous delays of the console versions were any indication, the developer will take all the time it needs to get it right.

Update, 9:55AM ET, November 19th: The SteamDB data cited now specifies that it’s concurrent users, not the number of users total.

India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed US robotics companies the data they need

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As demand grows for real-world data to train robots, India’s Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to help U.S.
  • In a recent development, the funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading.
  • Companies around the world are trying to build robots capable of performing everyday human tasks, but getting enough quality data to train them remains difficult.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As demand grows for real-world data to train robots, India’s Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to help U.S. AI and robotics companies build models that can operate in physical environments.

In a recent development, the funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading. It also includes $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.

Companies around the world are trying to build robots capable of performing everyday human tasks, but getting enough quality data to train them remains difficult. Startups, including Mecka AI, XDOF, and MicroAGI, are already tackling the problem by collecting real-world data for robotics training. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs aims to compete with them.

Humyn Labs has developed its own two-camera hardware to record people performing everyday tasks. It then uses its software to process and label the footage, which means tagging what happens in each clip so AI can learn from it. The startup collects data across over 20 countries in Latin America and Asia, with Brazil, India, and South Korea serving as its main hubs, co-founder Manish Agarwal (pictured above, right) said in an interview.

Sources indicate that agarwal, the former CEO of Indian gaming company Nazara Technologies, founded Humyn Labs in February with Ishank Gupta (pictured above, left), a former executive at the brewing giant AB InBev. The duo previously founded Kratos Studios, now known as KGeN. KGeN has a network of contributors across emerging markets, and that network helps Humyn Labs collect data in people’s homes, the founders told TechCrunch.

In a recent development, collecting footage of human activity is only part of the challenge, Agarwal stated. He added that Humyn Labs also uses software to track hand movements, interactions with objects, and other details, turning raw recordings into data that AI models can learn from.

“Scale, diversity, and quality are vital aspects, and they need to work in tandem,” Agarwal said.

It has been revealed that humyn Labs indicates it has 12 paying customers, including frontier AI labs, robotics companies, and developers of world models. About 90% of its revenue comes from the U.S., Gupta noted, though he declined to name specific customers.

The startup generated $10 million in revenue between April and October and has another $20 million in signed contracts, Agarwal told TechCrunch, adding that a further $20 million in deals has yet to be finalized.

According to recent reports, that growth has also increased Humyn Labs’ need for working capital, Agarwal said, explaining the $21 million venture debt component. The startup pays workers and data collection partners daily or weekly but typically waits 30 to 60 days to receive payments from its AI lab customers. Borrowing helps bridge that gap and is less dilutive than selling more equity, he said.

Industry observers note that over the last few months, India has emerged as a hub for collecting training data for so-called physical AI, with startups, including Human Archive and BuildAI, tapping into the country’s large workforce to record people performing everyday tasks. However, the practice has also raised questions about privacy and consent, particularly when people are recorded inside their homes.

According to recent reports, agarwal said Humyn Labs collects data from people doing their usual work or household chores instead of asking them to perform staged activities. The startup works with local partners to identify collection sites and oversee the process. “The worker is a worker who is incentivized, but he needs to be monitored and supervised for the right input,” he stated.

Humyn Labs presently has 51 full-time employees, most based in Bengaluru, plus a network of local partners across the countries where it collects data, Agarwal mentioned.

  • Ubisoft has enacted another round of mass layoffs, affecting 166 additional jobs as the French gaming giant continues its cost-cutting program.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ubisoft has enacted another round of mass layoffs, affecting 166 additional jobs as the French gaming giant continues its cost-cutting program. The job cuts are happening at two of Ubisoft's biggest development hubs in Montreal and Quebec. A spokesperson for Ubisoft mentioned the job cuts are coming to meet changing production needs, and IGN reported that the layoffs came from teams working on projects that have been "canceled or refocused." "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect," the spokesperson said. "Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources." Ubisoft Montreal is currently working on Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe, while Ubisoft Quebec most recently rolled out Assassin's Creed Shadows. No further updates are coming to that game, leaving the question of what the team is making next. In October, Ubisoft said there are no additional Assassin's Creed remakes currently in development, following the release of Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Resynced earlier this year. “Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin’s Creed titles, including projects you haven’t heard about yet, featuring fresh settings and stories," the developer said. Ubisoft's restructuring has led to several canceled games, shut-down studios, and layoffs. Trials developer RedLynx is on the chopping block, while 72 people from Ubisoft Singapore–the studio behind Skull & Bones–were recently laid off. Just today, November 19, Ubisoft released its latest earnings report that mentioned that Ubisoft's third phase of its cost-reduction program remains "firmly on track." Ubisoft is targeting €1.25 billion ($1.37 billion) in cost reductions by March 2028, so it's possible there will be more pain in the company's future.

Ubisoft Montreal is right now working on Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe, while Ubisoft Quebec most recently launched Assassin's Creed Shadows. No further updates are coming to that game, leaving the question of what the team is making next.

In October, Ubisoft stated there are no additional Assassin's Creed remakes presently in development, following the release of Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Resynced earlier this year.

“Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin’s Creed titles, including projects you haven’t heard about yet, featuring latest settings and stories," the developer mentioned.

Ubisoft's restructuring has led to several canceled games, shut-down studios, and layoffs. Trials developer RedLynx is on the chopping block, while 72 people from Ubisoft Singapore–the studio behind Skull & Bones–were recently laid off.

Just today, November 19, Ubisoft released its latest earnings report that mentioned that Ubisoft's third phase of its cost-reduction program remains "firmly on track." Ubisoft is targeting €1.25 billion ($1.37 billion) in cost reductions by March 2028, so it's possible there will be more pain in the manufacturer's future.

#15. Young people may be holding back gender equality at work

Young people may be holding back gender equality at work

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that about two decades ago, a substantial body of academic research started to provide evidence for what many had long suspected: young people were leading the way toward a more gender-equal world.
  • About two decades ago, a substantial body of academic research started to provide evidence for what many had long suspected: young people were leading the way toward a more gender-equal world.
  • European Social Survey data from 2004 and 2010 found that younger adults were considerably less likely than their older counterparts to endorse traditional gender roles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that about two decades ago, a substantial body of academic research started to provide evidence for what many had long suspected: young people were leading the way toward a more gender-equal world. European Social Survey data from 2004 and 2010 found that younger adults were considerably less likely than their older counterparts to endorse traditional gender roles. In 2009, Pew found that Americans under the age of 30 were considerably more liberal in their attitudes toward women’s roles than older generations. And in 2015, a study published in Psychology of Women Quarterly, found that millennials held more egalitarian attitudes toward women’s work and family roles than baby boomers had at the same age. The direction of travel seemed clear: each new generation was broadly more supportive of gender equality than the last. Over the last few years, though, there’s been a disconcerting shift. In several recent surveys, young men — and in some cases young women — have expressed more traditional attitudes toward gender roles, and greater scepticism about efforts to advance women’s equality, than men old enough to be their fathers or grandfathers. And there’s evidence that this generational divide extends to attitudes toward leadership, too. This month, the Reykjavík Index for Leadership — an annual study conducted by research firm Verian and the Reykjavík Global Foundation, a non-profit — found that younger adults are considerably less likely than their older counterparts to believe women and men are equally suited to lead. “The assumptions around sociodemographics and values and attitudes that we were able to make until the 2020s no longer hold in the same way,” states Michelle Harrison, president of Verian and co-founder of the index. “We understand we are in a new geopolitical and technological paradigm.” The findings raise troubling questions for businesses that have spent decades working to advance gender equality: what happens when the next generation of leaders appears less convinced of its importance than the last? And what can organizations do to change people’s minds? Growing generational divide Launched in 2018, the Reykjavík Index measures perceptions of gender-equal leadership across 23 sectors, from politics to technology. Its latest survey questioned more than 11,000 adults across the G7 — Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States — and four other countries, asking whether men, women or both are equally suited to lead. A score of 100 represents universal agreement that men and women are equally suited to leadership. After reaching a peak of 73 in 2019, the G7’s overall index score has steadily declined. This year, it edged up for the first time in seven years, rising one point to 69. But the modest recovery masks a real generational divide. Across the G7, 18- to 34-year-olds recorded an index score of just 65, compared with 74 among 55- to 65-year-olds. The gap itself is not new — it has existed since the index was launched in 2018 — but it has tripled from three to nine points in that time, and the youngest group’s score has also fallen five points over the same period. The divide is particularly stark in Britain and France, where younger adults trail their older counterparts by 14 points. And while young men’s attitudes have shown signs of improvement in several countries over the past year, the broader picture remains troubling. Younger adults are still the least likely to view men and women as equally suited to lead. These findings corroborate other studies. In 2025, a 30-country study by Ipsos and King’s College London found that Gen Z men and women were more divided on questions of feminism, gender roles and women’s rights than any other generation surveyed. Some 57% of Gen Z men agreed that efforts to promote women’s equality had gone so far that they discriminated against men, compared with 36% of Gen Z women and 44% of baby boomer men. The power of the manosphere Experts offer different explanations for what has caused the generational shift in attitudes. Many, however, mention social media’s ability to shape cultural scripts. “Contemporary online communities such as the manosphere are vocally opposed to women behaving in agentic or assertive ways. This includes in the home and in the workplace,” says Rachael Robnett, a professor of psychology and director of the Women’s Research Institute of Nevada at the University of Nevada. “To the extent that young men are disproportionately engaged in the manosphere relative to other generations, it makes sense that they would show less positive attitudes about women’s leadership ability,” she adds. Jess Carbino, a sociologist and author, agrees. “I believe the generational divide may reflect cyclical changes happening in how feminism and gender roles are being signalled in the media, particularly on social media,” she says. Another possibility, Carbino suggests, is that we’re witnessing a backlash against changing economic and social norms. The share of women who earn as much as — or significantly more than — their husbands has approximately tripled over the past 50 years, according to Pew data. For a brief period earlier this year, there were more women in non-farm payroll jobs in the U.S. than men, according to federal data. These changes have challenged longstanding assumptions about men as breadwinners and women as caregivers, and for some men, Carbino suggests, that shift can feel threatening. “When masculinity feels threatened — by earning less than a partner, for example, or by losing status at work — some men withdraw from domains culturally coded as feminine, like caregiving and housework,” she explains. Such responses can reinforce the very stereotypes that gender-equality initiatives have sought to dismantle: assumptions about who should lead a manufacturer, who should earn the family income and who should stay home to raise children. Related to this, Kent Bausman, a professor of sociology at Maryville University of Saint Louis, says that economic pressure and economic insecurity can “breed a sense of zero-sum gain in the competition for jobs and resources.” Young men who are “still socialized as the traditional economic provider interpret women’s expansion in opportunities across various walks of life as a threat to their own economic prospects,” he adds. A workplace opportunity For Harrison, the latest findings present employers with both a challenge and an opportunity. While the generational divide threatens to complicate efforts to advance gender equality, workplaces may also be among the most key settings in which attitudes can change. Unlike the online spaces where young people may encounter rigid ideas about masculinity and femininity, workplaces can expose them to different models of leadership, collaboration and authority. Seeing women succeed in senior positions, and men thrive in roles traditionally associated with women, help challenge assumptions about who is suited to lead. Carbino argues that employers can make those examples more visible and create opportunities for employees to learn from leaders who defy traditional expectations. “Employers can elevate and highlight women’s leadership,” she says. “They can engage in programs in which women mentor both men and women.” Ultimately, Carbino remains hopeful that the “pendulum will swing back.” Historically, she notes, periods of backlash against feminism have often been followed by renewed progress. Robnett, too, cautions against interpreting the findings as evidence that an entire generation has rejected gender equality. Although some young men hold more traditional attitudes than their older counterparts, not all of them do. “Although we need to continue to push for change in these negative attitudes, it is encouraging that most young men perceive women and men as equally suited to leadership roles,” she says. Indeed, there are tentative signs of progress: the G7’s overall index score has begun to recover, and young men’s scores have risen in five of the seven countries surveyed. Whether that recovery lasts remains uncertain, says Harrison. But, she says, the findings suggest that the next generation’s attitudes toward gender equality are not set in stone — and that the workplaces they enter could help shape what comes next.

Latest Update: I Used to Counteroffer My Best Employees With More Money. Now I Rely on These 3 Strategies.

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (983 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Entrepreneur

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • According to recent reports, like all business leaders, I have had some of my top performers tell me they were leaving.
  • According to statistics reported by HR Morning, replacing an employee costs upwards of 200% of what they were making.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

According to recent reports, like all business leaders, I have had some of my top performers tell me they were leaving. There is no way to sugarcoat the feeling. It’s like a kick in the belly — and in the wallet.

According to statistics reported by HR Morning, replacing an employee costs upwards of 200% of what they were making. And that is probably a conservative figure, given that losing a valuable team member can cause a ripple of lowered productivity and tabled projects as people scramble to pick up the ex-employee’s work.

Sources indicate that given these facts, I used to follow the standard pattern of attempting to keep talented team members by offering them higher compensation, bonuses or company equity. It was a tactic that almost always worked, but it didn’t create loyalty. Instead, it made those people price-sensitive, and they eventually found organizations willing to pay more, so they left anyway.

Sources indicate that I am not suggesting that it is wrong to counteroffer someone’s resignation with money. However, it’s reactive and arbitrary. Unless you have put a cap on how high you are willing to go, your negotiations will begin to feel like a moving target that’s out of your control. Again, you may end up delaying someone’s departure, but you won’t keep them forever unless you put more proactive measures in place.

According to recent reports, some positions in your firm drive enterprise value and some don’t. McKinsey and Company suggested in an older article that these will probably make up about 5% of your workforce — and contribute 800% more than others across your organization.

Over the years, I’ve found that I could typically name fewer than 10 roles that would materially impact my business if they remained vacant for an extended period. My recommendation is to name those roles and then create retention plans for each of them.

It has been revealed that what are some focused plan ideas? Deferred compensation structures allow team members to grow their money tax-free as long as they stay with your organization. That way, you won’t inflate your overall payroll and can concentrate your resources where they matter most. This type of long-term incentive can be tangibly meaningful because it’s tied to tenure and not merely performance. Since it’s only applicable to a small group of high-value employees, you aren’t raising your compensation across your organization, either.

I once considered using equity as a major retention lever. Why not? It felt right and seemed to be a no-brainer way to get people to stick around and contribute to our company’s growth. Yet when I mapped out the risks and rewards, I realized that giving away equity has massive long-term costs.

Here’s the issue: equity permanently dilutes your ability to use equity in other ways later. For example, you can’t bargain with equity with potential investors if a chunk of it has been given to your employees. Going the equity route also complicates your organizational governance, which can make your financial picture blurry.

Industry observers note that rather than offering equity to someone who wants to leave, explore non-equity alternatives. Treat equity as a last resort that you’ll only consider if you think it will bring out an employee’s long-term ownership behavior. And be open to talking about this with a professional who has helped other businesses design executive benefit and compensation structures that retain key people while protecting tax exposure and equity. Looking for a resource to get your feet wet? Colin Steinberg, a partner at Institutional Architects, frequently shares advice on executive planning and related topics.

According to recent reports, there are many business-friendlier alternatives to simply handing an employee who’s about to leave more money or equity. As mentioned before, you might provide deferred compensation, a way to delay income that benefits both you and the team member.

You might also look into supplemental executive retirement intends. Chances are strong that you already offer retirement benefits. Could you offer additional ones directly tied to both tenure and performance? Supplemental executive retirement plans help C-suite employees see meaningful future value in putting down roots, which SmartAsset explains can help trim churn among your highest-paid performers.

Sources indicate that when structured appropriately, these types of retention strategies avoid immediate financial strain on your balance sheet. They also allow you to turn retention tools into ways to improve your tax efficiency, reduce volatile compensation models and retain control over your equity.

According to recent reports, I firmly believe that founders who lose their most valuable people (but are otherwise building solid, fair companies) don’t have a problem with their retention. They have a problem with the way they’ve structured their long-term compensation packages for their most impactful roles. If you want to get real leverage as an employer, you need to develop smarter systems that incentivize your key players without losing your ground.

According to statistics reported by HR Morning, replacing an employee costs upwards of 200% of what they were making. And that is probably a conservative figure, given that losing a valuable team member can cause a ripple of lowered productivity and tabled projects as people scramble to pick up the ex-employee’s work.

According to recent reports, given these facts, I used to follow the standard pattern of attempting to keep talented team members by offering them higher compensation, bonuses or firm equity. It was a tactic that almost always worked, but it didn’t create loyalty. Instead, it made those people price-sensitive, and they eventually found organizations willing to pay more, so they left anyway.

WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that world of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's newly introduced items, class changes, and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that world of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices. In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's latest items, class changes, and more. On the subject of raid gear and chase items, Forever senior game designer Aidan Moon mentioned something that could be seen as controversial in certain circles of the game's community. "I essentially want to get rid of BiS," Moon said. "I think that BiS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about [the] role-playing aspects of it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=67dDe3QgJtM BiS is WoW shorthand for essentially the best item that could possibly be in a given gear slot for a specific class. Look up any WoW guide for WoW Classic or modern WoW, and you'll find class BiS gear lists telling players exactly what they should be wearing in order for their character to be as powerful as possible. Endgame in many ways revolves around acquiring your BiS gear, first your "pre-raid" BiS from gear available in max-level dungeons, and then BiS gear, like tier sets, from raids. It's for that exact reason Forever introduced new items that grant additional stats or effects against certain enemy types or even in certain locations. Moon gave an example of specific items that deal more damage against Murloc enemies, and that players might want to have more gear tailored to fighting against a Murloc boss in a raid encounter. Forever's raids will feature multiple distinct biomes within them, Moon revealed, giving players more factors to consider when choosing what gear to use for specific parts of each raid. One wing of a raid may be snowy, while another may be cavernous, changing what gear could be more optimal for those encounters. "I think your BiS should be different [for] every single boss if you're actually making a theoretical BiS list," Moon said. "It should be based on the creature and the biome and a mixture of those two. You might have an item that's really good against snowy, and then another item in that same slot that's really good against Murlocs. Then there's a Murloc boss in a snowy area and you're just like 'Which one do I wear?' And then eventually you get to a point where you're swapping those things out or it's too much cognitive load and you don't want to do that. It's for those players that really want to optimize."  Trying to get rid of BiS lists is a big change for WoW, which has revolved around the idea for over two decades. Players can already encounter some of the itemization ideas Moon discussed while leveling to 60, with low-level gear from dungeons and quests dealing more damage against specified enemy types or even granting additional movement speed in specific zones. "I don't want you to have to ever think about BiS, I just want you to think about the fight right in front of you and how you're going to fight it," Moon said. Of course, having more biome- or enemy-type-specific items means hoarding more pieces of gear as opposed to selling old ones when an upgrade comes around. That will no doubt rapidly fill up the inventories and banks of players looking to min-max for every possible scenario. Classic WoW is already notorious for having limited bag space, and players running around with multiple sets of hyper-specific gear will only make that pain point worse. Blizzard sounds like it's aware of that problem. Principal game designer Kris Zierhut said bigger bags are on that way, but that it's not needed right now immediately post-launch. However, Blizzard knows players will eventually need more bag space as well as better ways to organize and search for owned items to make putting together encounter-specific sets of gear easier. It's a massive change, but the strategy Blizzard is employing seems to be working. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent and weekly player records, and more than 15 million characters have been created in the MMO so far. College may cost much less than you think, according to this calculator tool from the University of Pennsylvania

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A quick Google search for the yearly cost of attending the University of Pennsylvania returns a flat figure: $99,082.
  • A quick Google search for the yearly cost of attending the University of Pennsylvania returns a flat figure: $99,082.
  • According to recent reports, but that remarkably high number doesn’t tell the full story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A quick Google search for the yearly cost of attending the University of Pennsylvania returns a flat figure: $99,082. But that remarkably high number doesn’t tell the full story. Nearly half of Penn students receive financial aid, with 68% of those students having all of their tuition and fees covered by need-based assistance. But prospective students and their families often don’t know whether they’ll fall into that group, instead daunted by the university’s projected $100,000 price tag. The uncertainty around the cost of college contributes to Gen Z’s declining interest in four-year degree programs. As of 2026, just 37% of college graduates say they believe their degree was worth the cost, while less than half of high school students in the U.S. (44%) say they expect to earn a bachelor’s degree. The latter stat, from a 2022 survey, marked a 20-year low for college expectations. That’s why Penn has joined a growing cohort of universities offering cost calculators to students, using information like family size and income to project a student’s cost of attendance long before they’re ever admitted. Calculator culture To use Penn’s cost calculator, prospective students and their parents input data from their tax forms (or the forms themselves) as well as information like their marital status and the number of college students in their family at the moment enrolled. The calculator then returns a four-year estimate of the cost for that student to attend Penn, taking into account their projected need-based aid. While the calculator takes time to return a result, it also offers a selection of sample families to compare with. Are you closer to Hana, whose family makes $37,000 and has 86% of her tuition covered by Penn, or Nathan, whose family makes $425,000 and is paying the full tuition cost themselves? Another college offering a cost calculator is Brandeis University, which launched a tool called FAYE (an acronym for “financial aid you can expect”) in May. Brandeis also offers academic merit-based aid, so FAYE takes students’ transcripts into account along with financial and family data. Other colleges offer less-sophisticated estimates of students’ annual costs, not with calculators, but with graphs. Take Yale’s instant net price estimator, which reveals a low, high, and best estimate of cost based on a family’s annual income. More than 60 other schools offer similar tools in collaboration with the College Board.

Tech Report: Felicis leads $7.5M bet on Unsiloed AI to make enterprise documents usable by AI agents

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge.
  • Silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures.
  • Business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge. Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to tackle that problem, aiming to help enterprises make their documents more accessible to AI agents through specialized technology.

Silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures. Angel investors Aarthi Ramamurthy and Beth Turner also participated.

Business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately. But getting the information wrong can lead to costly mistakes for businesses, and the impact could be severe in the case of a bank, hospital, or a law firm, as they rely on these documents for their daily work.

Unsiloed aims to solve this problem with software that breaks down complex documents, extracts information from tables, charts, and other elements, and turns it into structured data that AI agents can use. The technology also indicates where the extracted information came from in the original document, so businesses can check the results rather than take the AI’s output at face value.

Sources indicate that “The problem with LLMs is they’re inherently probabilistic,” mentioned Unsiloed co-founder and CEO Aman Mishra (pictured above, right) in an interview. “There is going to be some deviation induced. There is going to be some hallucination involved, and that has a massive negative impact downstream.”.

Recent findings suggest that mishra co-founded Unsiloed with Adnan Abbas (pictured above, left), his former classmate at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur. The two joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch after spending some time developing the technology.

It has been revealed that unsiloed is already working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare, Mishra told TechCrunch. One bank is using its technology to process documents, while a law firm has deployed it on its own servers to handle contracts and old case files, he said, without naming either customer. Mishra, however, named voice AI startup Bolna AI as a customer, saying it uses Unsiloed to ingest knowledge bases for building voice agents.

Sources indicate that the San Francisco-headquartered startup has entered a market that is already crowded and includes specialized document-processing startups such as Reducto and Unstructured, as well as offerings from Microsoft and Amazon. Businesses also sometimes use general-purpose AI models to extract information from documents, giving Unsiloed another set of competitors.

Mishra told TechCrunch that Unsiloed’s advantage lies in how it processes complex documents. The startup uses what it calls “dual-stream” vision models, which handle text and image data separately, along with a technique called “heat map-based chunking” that helps identify the most notable parts of a document.

In a recent development, “In one of the streams you have the text tokens, in the other stream you have the exact image tokens,” Mishra said. “This is something that we have spent a lot of time architecting.”.

In a recent development, the technology then directs more computing power toward areas such as figures, numbers, and charts. Unsiloed also uses a specialized decoder that takes industry-specific terminology into account, helping it distinguish between terms that can mean different things in different business contexts.

Industry observers note that supporting those claims, Mishra pointed to a test involving 542 financial documents supplied by an enterprise customer. Unsiloed achieved 99.78% accuracy across roughly 84,000 extracted data points, per a technical brief shared by the startup. The test compared Unsiloed with major AI models, Microsoft’s Azure Document Intelligence, and the customer’s in-house extraction tool. The results have, however, not been independently verified.

Recent findings suggest that unsiloed also claims to have outperformed competing AI document-processing tools on olmOCR-Bench, a public benchmark developed by Allen AI. In tests conducted by the startup, Unsiloed scored 88.0, compared with 66.0 for Reducto’s agentic system and 39.9 for Unstructured. The benchmark covered 1,403 PDF pages and tested how well the systems handled tables, mathematical expressions, scanned documents, and complex layouts.

In a recent development, unsiloed’s pricing, Mishra mentioned, starts at one cent per page. He asserted that the startup’s approach also helps keep its costs down by directing computing power toward the parts of a document that need the most attention, instead of processing every section in the same way.

Sources indicate that currently, Unsiloed has a headcount of seven people. The startup, Mishra said, aims to use the fresh funding to hire more researchers and engineers, expand its sales efforts, and develop proprietary datasets to improve its technology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The console’s latest enhancement finally activates its dormant Wi-Fi hardware, enabling a handful of new features.

The console’s latest update finally activates its dormant Wi-Fi hardware, enabling a handful of fresh features.

Analogue has long been good at expanding the features and functionality of its consoles through regular firmware updates, but installing those updates has always required moving files around with a memory card. That’s no longer the case with the Analogue 3D, the tech giant’s modernized version of the Nintendo 64. Although the console has had Wi-Fi hardware since day one, it’s only now been finally activated through the last upgrade you’ll need to install with a memory card.

In a recent development, analogue on Wednesday released the version 1.6.0 firmware for the Analogue 3D, adding support for 2.4GHz, 5GHz, mixed, and hidden Wi-Fi networks. Once the update is installed, the Wi-Fi setup process will begin automatically when the console is booted, but there’s now an added Wi-Fi section in the Analogue 3D’s settings menu for updating passwords and other details later.

It has been revealed that the console’s new Wi-Fi capabilities add a couple of useful features at launch. In the future, the Analogue 3D will be able to download and install firmware updates so it automatically keeps itself up to date. The new wireless capabilities enable automatic date and time settings based on your time zone, too, and in the privacy section of the console’s settings menu, you’ll now find an option for sharing “anonymous usage and analytics data” with Analogue to help further improve its hardware.

#7. How to manage a post-IPO workforce that just became fabulously wealthy

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1748 w)

How to manage a post-IPO workforce that just became fabulously wealthy

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic’s $1.5 trillion initial public offering instantly turned thousands of its roughly 5,300 employees into multimillionaires.
  • Anthropic’s $1.5 trillion initial public offering instantly turned thousands of its roughly 5,300 employees into multimillionaires.
  • Sources indicate that like other companies that have undergone massive IPOs, Anthropic is now facing a challenge: how to keep the trains running with a workforce where many employees may no longer need to work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic’s $1.5 trillion initial public offering instantly turned thousands of its roughly 5,300 employees into multimillionaires. Like other companies that have undergone massive IPOs, Anthropic is now facing a challenge: how to keep the trains running with a workforce where many employees may no longer need to work. Indeed, studies show that employees at post-IPO companies are more likely to leave their jobs or become less satisfied. Management experts and executives who have successfully navigated IPOs say there are a few ways companies can make sure that doesn’t happen. GIVE EMPLOYEES A REASON TO WORK OTHER THAN MONEY The most important thing is to make sure workers have a sense of purpose that goes beyond making money, something Google cofounders Larry Page and Sergey Brin highlighted explicitly in a letter to prospective shareholders when the company went public in 2004. “Talented people are attracted to Google because we empower them to change the world,” they wrote. “We are focused on providing an environment where talented, hardworking people are rewarded for their contributions to Google and for making the world a better place.” Laszlo Bock, who oversaw Google’s human resources operations for a decade following its IPO, echoed that sentiment nearly 10 years later. “We spend more time working than we do on almost any other activity in our lives,” he wrote. “People want all that time to mean something.” Of course, it is ideal if that sense of purpose is already in place before a company goes public. “If a company’s employees are coming to work just to make money, it’s over,” venture capitalist Paul Koontz stated in 2004. “There need to be some bigger ambitions, some more fundamental calling that motivates a company.” GIVE WOULD-BE ENTREPRENEURS FREEDOM TO EXPERIMENT One of the biggest risks for post-IPO companies is that their most talented and entrepreneurial employees now have the resources to launch their own ventures. In fact, the effect is so powerful that at least one study has identified a causal link between the rate of IPOs in the economy and the rate of newly introduced firm creation. While it may be impossible to prevent these exits altogether, post-IPO companies should ensure that their most talented staff have the freedom and resources to pursue their own ideas. “There has to be safe space for entrepreneurial employees,” Syracuse University professor Carl Schramm said in 2018. “There has to be some space where people can actually try and push an idea around, scope it out, have a friendly ear someplace in the hierarchy of the company.” Management should also consider giving top talent their own discretionary research budgets. In the mid-2010s, Adobe rolled out a program that gave its workers $1,000 to spend however they liked, with no explanation or justification required. “When you trust people, they’ll live up to your expectations,” Mark Randall, formerly Adobe’s chief strategist and VP of creativity, told Fast Company. “They’ll allocate their resources and figure out how to move ahead.” DON’T LET WEALTH CREATE A NEW OFFICE HIERARCHY IPOs can create an awkward social dynamic in which employees’ wealth bears little relationship to their seniority, or even their contributions to the company. This can leave managers supervising employees who have several times their network, and newcomers resenting colleagues who got rich doing the same basic job. Post-IPO companies should acknowledge this dynamic instead of pretending it doesn’t exist. Ahead of Google’s IPO, clinical psychologist Steven Goldbart recommended that companies organize workshops for employees to discuss how their newfound wealth affects workplace relationships, job expectations, and corporate culture. “The biggest mistake a company can make is to pretend [an IPO] has no impact,” he said. Executive compensation consultants Todd Sirras and Austin Vanbastelaer also recommend giving managers more power to reward top performers, including by “increasing responsibilities, expanding strategic opportunities, and promoting visibility and engagement with senior executives.” PAY ATTENTION TO WELL-BEING AND WORKING CONDITIONS Employees at startups often put up with grueling hours and difficult work conditions knowing they may be in line for a big payoff. Once the payoff arrives, however, their tolerance for those things may go away. And new stressors will also emerge, including increased bureaucracy, regulatory burdens, and the pressure to meet quarterly earnings. Indeed, one study that analyzed 3.7 million Glassdoor reviews found that employee ratings of senior management and work-life balance declined by 10% and 6.6% following IPOs. Post-IPO companies must keep their finger on the pulse of their workforce to identify any percolating dissent. For example, in the run-up to Google’s 2004 IPO, Silicon Valley executive coach Laura Steck advised companies preparing to go public to survey employees about how to improve working conditions. Management may also simply need to take their foot off the gas pedal a little bit. In one study, published earlier this year, researchers from the University of Alabama and the University of Iowa examined the management practices and long-term survival of 183 companies that went public in 1996. They found that companies are more likely to survive if executives strike the right balance between maintaining a sense of urgency and valuing employees. “Too little sense of urgency can lead to complacency while too much urgency can lead to burnout, lower quality output, and other undesirable consequences,” the authors wrote.

GTA 6 is now available worldwide, so the numbers are expected to continue to climb higher. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick remarked on TBPN today that the company is going to share official sales data for GTA 6 soon, so it may not be much longer until we get some hard data directly from the source. The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 18.44 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 6.15 million on Xbox Series X|S. In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.77 billion in revenue, compared to $588 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies. The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0FOR4_lSvJs Sensor Tower projected as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and that prediction is looking pretty accurate. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator. Circana has released latest data that highlights that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game. GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. According to recent reports, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Valve revealed some updates about Steam Machine availability today, including good news if you want to buy one right now and potential bad news about future supply due to RAMaggedon.

According to recent reports, the good news: You can now purchase a 512GB Steam Machine without getting on a waitlist. Initially, interested buyers had to get on Valve’s waitlist if they wanted to purchase one, but the console-like PC is now available in an “add-to-cart” status, according to the company. As I write this, the 512GB versions with and without a bundled controller are showing estimated delivery dates of three to five business days on Valve’s website. If Valve sells through its current inventory, the company notes it will indicate that the product is out of stock instead of making another waitlist.

Sources indicate that the bad news: If you’re on the waitlist for a 2TB model, you might not get a chance to buy one at all, as Valve says there are more people on the waitlist than there are units available. The manufacturer is closing the waitlists for its 2TB models.

Valve says that while it’s still building more Steam machines, “memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels” and that it doesn’t know the number it can make or “at what price we’ll be able to offer them.” The 2TB Steam Machine is “especially constrained.” The firm anticipates “having more information” to share about additional supply in January.

Industry observers note that after delaying the Steam Machine’s expected early 2026 launch due to the memory and storage crisis, Valve introduced the product in June with a price starting at $1,049 for the 512GB model without a bundled controller. A 2TB model without a controller costs $1,349.

It has been revealed that U.K.-based fintech Payhawk declared a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted. The round values the manufacturer at $2 billion, bringing its total funding to more than $500 million to date.

Founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents. Speaking to FinTech magazine, Payhawk’s co-founder and CEO, Hristo Borisov, said the tech giant saw “an incredible growth opportunity and room to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls.”.

According to recent reports, payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and states it operates in 33 countries. Notably, the firm remarked it still has 70% of the $100 million it raised in 2022, a round that valued the company at $1 billion. This fresh capital will support its global expansion. Other investors in the round include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED.

Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
